title: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Drug resistance in
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    (
                    Mtb
                    ) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links
                    ppe1
                    mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the
                    Mtb
                    Δ
                    ppe1
                    mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δ
                    ppe1
                    strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing
                    Mtb
                    physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

title: An innervated and vascularized HNSCC-on-a-chip model built on defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Understanding the tumor microenvironment requires experimental platforms that faithfully recapitulate its key components. Here, we present an innervated and vascularized head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)-on-a-chip platform built with fully defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices (eECMs). In a stepwise increase of complexity, we first cocultured patient-derived HNSCC cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and endothelial cells within tailored eECMs, revealing extracellular matrix-dependent differences in transcriptional state, multicellular self-organization, and chemotherapeutic sensitivity. We then integrated these three-dimensional constructs into a cancer–vasculature interface, which enabled analysis of eECM-dependent directional collective migration and invasion. Finally, we incorporated trigeminal innervation through injectable 3D human bioengineered trigeminal ganglia, establishing a chip-based innervation–tumor–vasculature tri-interface. Together, this all-human platform integrates fully defined ECM, vasculature, and innervation in a single modular system to investigate tumor organization, invasion, and therapeutic responses within a controlled human microenvironment.

title: VAP organizes presynaptic Ca2+ signaling and synaptic vesicle mobilization through Kv2 membrane contact sites
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In neurons, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) forms an extensive network that establishes membrane contact sites (MCSs) with various organelles including the plasma membrane (PM). While MCSs are known to regulate lipid exchange and Ca
                    2+
                    signaling, their specific roles in synaptic transmission remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the ER-resident proteins VAPA and VAPB are essential for organizing presynaptic Ca
                    2+
                    exchange and mobilizing synaptic vesicles. We show that the loss of VAP impairs Ca
                    2+
                    loading into both the ER and mitochondria during electrical activity. This regulation occurs primarily through VAP interactions with voltage-gated potassium (Kv2) channels at the PM. Our data suggest that the Kv2–VAP complex organizes presynaptic Ca
                    2+
                    signaling outside the active zone. Without this scaffold, vesicle mobilization for exocytosis is strongly impaired and a larger fraction remains trapped in the reserve pool. These findings reveal a role for Kv2–VAP MCSs in coordinating organelle Ca
                    2+
                    signaling and the synaptic vesicle cycle.

title: Protein resource allocation across subcellular compartments revealed by large-scale absolute quantitative proteomics in yeast
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Subcellular compartmentalization within complex membrane-bound organelles is a hallmark of eukaryal life, enabling metabolic specialization through spatial segregation. Here, we compiled a dataset encompassing 300 absolute quantitative proteomes, the largest to date, across two yeast species under diverse experimental conditions. Leveraging big data analysis, formula fitting, and machine learning, quantitative correlations among protein abundance, resource allocation, and cellular phenotypes were elucidated at a system level. We found that subcellular resource distribution is highly uneven and covaries with specific growth rate. Specifically, at high specific growth rates, the protein mass fraction (PMF) from certain compartments, (e.g., nucleus) is consistently reduced, coinciding with the increasing protein resource demand from ribosomes. Meanwhile, nutrient limitation may induce resource recycling by upregulating protein resources within specific compartments (e.g., vacuole) to sustain stress adaptation. Importantly, our integrative analysis indicates that PMF from a few subcellular compartments (e.g., nucleus and ribosomes) can accurately predict yeast physiological parameters (e.g., specific growth rate, oxygen uptake rate), and a limited protein set (≥ 23) could be used to capture the variation in resource allocation across seven major subcellular compartments. Furthermore, our comparative analysis between Crabtree-positive and Crabtree-negative species across conditions illustrates that subcellular resource allocation could be shaped by multiple factors and the two species differ markedly in their robustness to environmental perturbations. In summary, the high-quality quantitative proteomic dataset for yeast species offers an unprecedented opportunity for understanding the general principles underlying subcellular resource allocation, laying foundations for precision engineering of cell factories in synthetic biology.

title: Imaging real-space chiral rotation of flat-band states in helical trilayer graphene
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Flat bands have been experimentally realized in a wide variety of graphene-based moiré systems with designed stacking configurations. While these moiré systems feature similar flat-band structures, they differ markedly in key characteristics, such as band flattening, band isolation, and band topology, which give rise to their distinct strongly correlated phases. Here, we present a systematic real-space investigation comparing flat-band states across four representative graphene moiré systems, revealing a characteristic chiral rotation of flat-band states within helical trilayer graphene. Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we directly observe that ultra-small twist-angle helical trilayer graphene unveils distinct threefold-anisotropic electronic states localized at certain moiré sites within the flat-band regime, distinguishing it from the other moiré systems investigated in this study. Spatial mapping of the threefold-anisotropic pattern reveals a chiral rotation that varies as a function of energy. Theoretical simulations based on the Bistritzer–MacDonald model reproduce the distinct orientations of the threefold-anisotropic patterns across different low-energy minibands and reveal a systematic correspondence between the direction of local density-of-states rotation and the structural chirality of helical trilayer graphene. Our results demonstrate that real-space electronic textures—previously overlooked—can partially reveal the intrinsic disparities among different flat bands, highlighting that systematic exploration of flat bands across moiré systems is critical for deciphering the origins of distinct correlated phases.

title: Capture and reduction of singlet oxygen via an anthracene-based framework for stable Li-O2 batteries
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Given the increasing global energy demand and rapid advancement of low-carbon technologies, Li-O
                    2
                    batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, offering great promise for advanced energy systems. However, the formation of harmful singlet oxygen (
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    ) in both discharge and charge processes induces parasitic reactions that deteriorate round-trip efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, an anthracene-based covalent-organic framework (AntCOF) is introduced as a highly effective catalyst for the
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    reduction reaction (SORR) in Li-O
                    2
                    batteries. The conjugated porous framework selectively captures electrophilic
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    , enabling effective charge transfer from AntCOF to the empty π* orbital of
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    and promoting SORR in subsequent discharge processes. This mechanism suppresses
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    diffusion and mitigates associated side reactions, leading to reduced overpotentials and improved cycling performance when coupled with a RuO
                    2
                    catalyst. This work may enlighten further investigations into
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    -related chemistry across a broad range of oxygen-redox electrochemical systems.

title: Regulation of miR-219 and its target RalGPS is essential for synaptic plasticity at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
RNA regulatory mechanisms mediate adaptive responses relying on rapid changes in gene expression. By examining microRNA (miRNA)-mediated control of structural synaptic plasticity, we find miR-219 and five other conserved miRNAs regulate activity-induced morphogenesis at
                    Drosophila
                    glutamatergic synapses. Among miRNA targets downregulated by acute stimulation, the Ral activating factor RalGPS is necessary for presynaptic morphogenesis and is sufficient to block plasticity. We find that RalGPS must be held within a narrow range of expression for structural remodeling to occur. Loss or excess of RalGPS both abolish activity-induced synapse growth. Without altering levels of mature miR-219, stimulation elevates miR-219 loading in Argonaute (Ago1)-containing complexes that mediate miRNA gene silencing. We also find that elevated Protein Kinase A activity suppresses miR-219 association with Ago1 and blocks activity-induced synaptic growth, suggesting that miRNA loading and unloading in neurons are both controlled by activity-dependent regulation of Ago1.

title: SMYD3-catalyzed dimethylation of gasdermin D at lysine 43 promotes pyroptosis and inflammatory responses
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Gasdermin D (GSDMD), a key pyroptosis effector downstream of inflammasome activation, undergoes precise regulation by multiple posttranslational modifications. Here, we identify SMYD3, a lysine methyltransferase, as a positive regulator of GSDMD. SMYD3 interacts with GSDMD and catalyzes its dimethylation at lysine 43. This modification promotes GSDMD cleavage by caspases, leading to increased oligomerization and membrane localization of GSDMD N-terminal fragment (GSDMD-NT), which ultimately induces pyroptosis. Disrupting or inhibiting SMYD3 alleviates overactivated inflammation, thereby protecting against lipopolysaccharide-induced death in mice and zebrafish. Our findings reveal a role for SMYD3 in regulating the inflammatory response and shed light on a new mechanism that modulates GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis.

title: Modeling a continuum of drug-induced persistence during targeted cancer therapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: We introduce a general phenomenological framework for understanding how phenotypic plasticity gives rise to drug persisters. These persisters, often quiescent but which sometimes return to cycling, survive in the presence of targeted therapy and eventually can lead to mutants with true resistance. Our framework builds on recent experimental observations regarding variations between and among single-cell clones and the possible role of the drug itself in enhancing the survival strategy. Predictions of our approach include the existence of an optimum drug concentration as well as an optimum drug holiday schedule to minimize the persistence-based threat.

title: Intraventricular clindamycin enhances interstitial brain fluid drainage and the blood–brain barrier after a traumatic brain injury
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Despite advances in the acute clinical management of severe traumatic brain injuries (TBIs), treating injury-derived secondary pathogenesis remains challenging. We demonstrate intracerebroventricular (I.C.V.) administration of clindamycin alleviates TBI secondary pathogenesis in both focal and diffuse murine models of brain injury. I.C.V. administration of clindamycin increased the motility of ependymal cilia, which line the ventricles and spinal canal, by 30 to 60%, which correlated with interstitial brain fluid drainage through the cortex (r > 0.9 Pearson, n = 4 compounds tested). I.C.V. clindamycin treatment post-TBI also restored the blood–brain barrier (BBB), decreased lesion size, and lowered serum levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein by 2.8-fold. Consistent with these data, a novel objective recognition test revealed an improvement in recognition memory in brain-injured mice treated with clindamycin. These collective findings reveal a counterintuitive finding that I.C.V. clindamycin enhances drainage of toxins from the brain while simultaneously restoring the BBB, potentially providing a new solution for alleviating secondary pathogenesis in brain-injured patients.

title: Calcium permeability–enhancing mutations in GluRIIC suppress sustained presynaptic homeostatic plasticity triggered by loss of GluRIIA
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Presynaptic homeostatic plasticity (PHP) stabilizes neural circuits by adjusting synaptic strength when faced with disturbances in postsynaptic activity. Despite identification of many genes and mechanisms required for PHP, the underlying trigger mechanisms remain elusive. Loss of GluRIIA, one of five glutamate receptor subunits at the
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction (NMJ), reduces quantal size and synaptic calcium influx and triggers a sustained PHP. Two common features of genetic manipulations that lead to the activation of this form of PHP are a drop in synaptic calcium influx and a reduction in quantal size; however, it is not clear that either of these features is absolutely necessary for PHP. We have generated a glutamate receptor transgene with mutations in the pore, which can largely restore calcium influx in
                    
                      GluRIIA
                      −/−
                    
                    mutant larvae without affecting quantal size. We find that restoration of calcium influx in
                    
                      GluRIIA
                      −/−
                    
                    mutant larvae blocks PHP without any detectable changes in synaptic structure. Our findings, therefore, indicate that a reduction in synaptic calcium influx is necessary for triggering and/or maintenance of the sustained PHP at the NMJ, a model that may be extendable to the vertebrate NMJ and neuron–neuron synapses.

title: Viral metagenomics reveals heterogeneity in mammalian virus hosting, sharing, and spillover
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Zoonotic viruses originating from mammals pose a persistent threat to global health. While rodents and bats are often considered “special reservoirs,” it is debated if spillover risk is driven by specific taxa or merely reflects mammalian species richness. However, most tests have focused on published host–virus association datasets, which can reflect systematic biases in host and virus sampling effort. To address this limitation, we analyzed a comprehensive repository of 4,685 metagenomic datasets, minimizing bias toward any one viral taxon and spanning 296 species across 14 mammalian orders. We characterized the global mammalian virome and found substantial heterogeneity in the capacity of different mammalian orders to harbor and share human-associated viruses. Counter to conventional wisdom, carnivores exhibited significantly higher propensities to carry human-associated viruses, with bats ranked lower in this metric of zoonotic risk. Network analyses of viral sharing further revealed higher cross-order virus sharing among specific mammalian orders (e.g., carnivores and artiodactyls). Phylogenetic comparative analyses revealed that host life-history traits (e.g., longevity) and anthropogenic factors (e.g., urban land use) were key ecological drivers of both virus richness and transmission centrality. Our study provides a data-driven framework that challenges prevailing narratives of zoonotic risk and offers a refined strategy for prioritizing surveillance and mitigating emerging zoonotic threats.

title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body’s glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.

title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log
                    10
                    at 3 mo postpartum, “controllers”) and 12 with more stable levels (“noncontrollers”). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure.

title: Stress-inducible WASF3 regulates brain metabolism and cognitive function
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome protein family member 3 (WASF3) disrupts mitochondrial respiration and is induced in association with endoplasmic reticulum stress in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Because cognitive impairment is a hallmark of ME/CFS, we investigated the role of WASF3 in brain metabolism and function using WASF3 transgenic and knockout mouse models. WASF3 disrupted respiratory complex IV and localized to mitochondria-associated membranes, known to modulate cellular processes important for neuronal activity. Overexpression of WASF3 in the hippocampus, a critical region for memory formation, induced a metabolic shift toward glycolysis and promoted a “hypometabolic” state. Increased WASF3 also caused a reduction in ATPIF1, previously shown to facilitate cognitive function, and impaired learning. Conversely, WASF3 deficiency increased ATPIF1 level, enhanced oxidative metabolism, and preserved cognitive function under stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that WASF3 suppresses oxidative metabolism in the brain and contributes to cognitive dysfunction, providing mechanistic insights into the “brain fog” reported in ME/CFS.

title: Holocene millennial climate variability influenced by tropical–Antarctic ocean–atmosphere interactions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: A prominent unstable feature, millennial-scale climate oscillation (MCO), punctuated the Holocene. Solar activity and deep ocean variability are generally regarded as the origin of the MCO, yet the dynamics remain debated. Using a Holocene transient simulation with the EC-Earth climate model (8 to 0 ka BP), together with a global compilation of 304 temperature reconstructions, here we identify a robust ~1,350-y oscillatory mode that characterizes Holocene climate variability and is self-sustained and crucially influenced by tropical–Antarctic ocean–atmosphere interactions. Within each cycle, Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) strengthening evolves with the developing warming and an El Niño-like tropical sea surface temperature (SST) response, accompanied by anticyclonic circulation anomalies over the high-latitude Southern Ocean. Northward cold advection of the associated enhanced westerly winds off the Antarctic coast overcomes the effect of sea ice retreat to promote AABW formation, ocean stratification, and warming. Positive feedbacks including sea ice-albedo, tropical air–sea interaction, and SST-AABW magnify surface warming till AABW reaches its peak. Thereafter, reduced brine rejection from sea-ice retreat weakens AABW, counteracts the warming, and commences a switch to its cooling phase. The dominant periodicity, consistent with that inferred from proxy reconstructions, is confirmed by complementary climate simulations. These results provide an alternative physical mechanism for Holocene millennial-scale climate variability. Under future anthropogenic warming, a positive phase of the oscillation may heighten the positive feedbacks, thereby increasing the risk of rapid climate transformation.

title: Septin binding restricts Shigella growth and triggers intracellular tolerance
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Pathogen survival relies on their ability to adapt to changing environments, yet how intracellular bacteria tolerate cell-autonomous immunity remains unclear. Septins assemble into cage-like structures around cytoplasmic
                    Shigella
                    targeted by autophagy, but their antibacterial activity was unknown. Using advanced microscopy and cell-free reconstitution, we show that septins polymerize into circumferentially oriented filaments that inhibit bacterial growth. RNA-sequencing reveals that septin binding to
                    Shigella
                    upregulates type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors and triggers a stress response. Underlying this, septin-bound
                    Shigella
                    possess hyperpolarized membranes, but without lethally damaged cell envelope. We show that exposure to septin binding enhances the impact of the cell envelope-targeting antibiotic polymyxin B. During infection, T3SS effector OspC1 prevents septin recruitment, while stress-response regulator
                    cspC
                    protects against septin-mediated changes to membrane potential. Hence, septin binding is intrinsically antibacterial and is sensed by
                    Shigella
                    as a danger signal to promote mechanisms of intracellular tolerance.

title: Synchronous end-Permian mass extinction zenith in marine and low–middle latitude terrestrial North China
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The end-Permian mass extinction was the most severe biotic crisis of the Phanerozoic, yet temporal synchrony between marine and terrestrial extinctions remains debated due to correlation uncertainties. Here, we present an integrated magnetostratigraphic, cyclostratigraphic, and carbon-isotope and mercury (Hg) chemostratigraphic record from the fluvial Upper Shihhotse, Sunjiagou, and Liujiagou formations at the Sigou section, North China. We identify 14 magnetozones spanning the late Changhsingian to late Olenekian, constrained by a floating timescale based on gamma-ray cyclostratigraphy and subsequently anchored through magnetostratigraphic correlation. Our chronostratigraphy reveals a Hg peak at 252.4 Ma, aligning with the main eruptive phase of the Siberian Traps Large Igneous Province, while the carbon isotope excursion onset (252.1 Ma) and minimum (252.0 Ma) are synchronous with the Meishan Global Stratotype Section and Point. Furthermore, the Induan–Olenekian boundary is positioned below magnetozone SG4n, constraining the Induan Stage duration to 1.6 to 1.8 My. These findings establish a high-resolution chronostratigraphic framework for the Permian–Triassic boundary in North China, supporting a synchronous extinction zenith across marine and low–middle latitude terrestrial ecosystems, with latitudinal diachroneity relative to high-latitude and tropical landmasses.

title: Revised estimates of types and duration of long COVID symptoms based on claims records from 245 million US patients
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: COVID-19 has been reported to cause multisystem effects lasting years [Z. Al-Aly, E. Topol, Science 383, 830–832 (2024)]. These findings are primarily based on cohort studies comparing test-positive COVID-19 patients to controls without known COVID-19 infection, tested or untested [M. Cai, Y. Xie, E. J. Topol, Z. Al-Aly, Nat. Med. 30, 1564–1573 (2024)]. However, such comparisons can be biased by the reasons people were tested. Using 14.4 billion insurance claims from 244.7 million US patients, we find that most long-term effects attributed to COVID-19 by unrestricted control designs likely reflect bias due to selective testing of individuals with non-COVID conditions, causing long-term effects of those conditions to be misattributed to COVID-19. We removed this bias by analyzing only tested individuals, comparing test-positive to test-negative patients. Across 614 clinical outcomes followed over 2 y, the test-based design resulted in 83.5% fewer symptoms being attributable to COVID-19 between 30 to 119 d after infection (43 attributable symptoms vs. 262 for the unrestricted control design), a 98.2% reduction at 120 to 359 d (5 vs. 286), and a 100% reduction at 360 to 719 d (0 vs. 369). The unrestricted control design also attributed unrelated outcomes (e.g., firearm injuries) to COVID-19 at a high rate, whereas the testing-based design did not. The test-based control design may modestly underestimate some effects. This study does not indicate that symptoms beyond one year are not genuine but that their attributability to COVID-19 is uncertain.

title: Neuromodulation-inspired gated associative memory networks: Extended memory retrieval and emergent multistability
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Classical autoassociative memory models have been central to understanding emergent computations in recurrent neural circuits across diverse biological contexts. However, they typically neglect neuromodulatory agents that are known to strongly shape memory capacity and stability. Here we introduce a minimal, biophysically motivated associative memory network in which neuromodulator-like signals are modeled by a self-adaptive, activity-dependent gating mechanism. Using many-body simulations and dynamical mean-field theory, we show that such gating fundamentally reorganizes the attractor structure: the network bypasses the classical spin-glass transition, maintaining robust, high-overlap retrieval far beyond the standard critical capacity. Mechanistically, when the gates act as fully open or fully closed switches, the gate stabilizes transient “ghost” remnants of stored patterns even far above the Hopfield limit, converting a single memory fixed-point attractor into a cluster of fixed points. The retrieved state is set by the initial overlap rather than quantized to the stored pattern. This graded dependence may be exploited for input-driven computation with persistent activity. These results establish that neuromodulation-like gating alone—without modifying synaptic weights or introducing explicit higher-order couplings—can dramatically expand memory capacity, eliminate catastrophic breakdown, and reshape a discrete attractor landscape into a rich continuum, suggesting a general and biologically accessible route to enhanced computational capabilities in neural circuits and neuromorphic architectures.

title: Mechanically driven grain refinement in Mo by nanoindentation pop-ins: A case of transient instability
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: During load-controlled nanoindentation of pristine metals, the homogeneous dislocation nucleation manifests as a sudden displacement burst, or pop-in, associated with shear stresses approaching the theoretical strength, massive dislocation nucleation, and rapid yet uncontrolled indenter penetration. Here, we show that manually terminating nanoindentation immediately after the first pop-in enables direct access to a transient deformation and reveals unexpected microstructural transformations in molybdenum (Mo). Using single-crystal Mo with different surface orientations, we demonstrate pop-in-induced nucleation of new, highly misoriented grains at room temperature. This nucleation behavior is attributed to two mechanically driven processes: 1) activation of twinning followed by the evolution of twin boundaries into random high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) and 2) rearrangement of dislocations into HAGBs within regions of high local dislocation density during the abrupt deformation accompanying the pop-in. Displacement-controlled atomistic simulations reproduce both twin- and dislocation-mediated grain nucleation within an individual grain when a preexisting grain boundary blocks dislocation glide. However, in the absence of such a grain boundary, nucleated dislocations glide into the surrounding crystal and fail to form new grains. Continued indentation beyond pop-in mechanically erases newly formed grains, as confirmed in both experiments and simulations, explaining why this phenomenon was not detected in previous studies. Together, the observed nucleation and subsequent erasure of the grains establish the nanoindentation pop-in as a simple, widely accessible platform for qualitatively probing transient microstructural evolution in defect-scarce metals.

title: Recognition-dependent activation of the Arabidopsis RRS1-R/RPS4 TIR-NLR immune receptor pair
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Plant TIR domain-containing proteins exhibit NADase activity upon pathogen effector recognition, creating small molecules that activate defense via EDS1 and its associated proteins.
                    Arabidopsis
                    RPS4 and RRS1 comprise a TIR-NLR immune receptor pair that recognizes multiple effector proteins including AvrRps4 and PopP2. We show here that RPS4 and RRS1 acquire NADase activity upon recognition of a cognate effector. However, both in the presence and absence of effector, RPS4 and RRS1 form an oligomer that does not change in size upon effector provision. Effector-dependent defense activation by RPS4 and RRS1 requires the catalytic glutamate residue and the BB-loop motif of RPS4, which is absent in RRS1 and other RRS1-like TIR domains in
                    Arabidopsis
                    . Oligomerization of RPS4 and RRS1 occurs through multiple domains, but oligomerization does not require enzymatic activity. We propose that conformational changes or reconfiguration within the RPS4/RRS1 oligomer upon effector recognition derepresses the complex for immune activation.

title: Annexins cooperate with Myomaker to promote myoblast fusion
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Myoblast fusion is essential for skeletal muscle development and regeneration. Myomaker is a muscle-specific fusogen indispensable for this process. Cryoelectron microscopy analysis has shown that Myomaker dimerization is required for myoblast fusion and muscle formation. However, the precise molecular mechanisms of Myomaker function remain unclear. Notably, the short extracellular domain of Myomaker suggests the involvement of additional proteins that cooperate with Myomaker to facilitate membrane fusion. To identify potential interacting partners of Myomaker, we employed an APEX2-based proximity labeling approach in a synchronized myoblast fusion and differentiation system. By comparing results with a fusion-deficient mutant form of Myomaker, we identified several members of the Annexin family of calcium-dependent phospholipid-binding proteins as prominent candidates for interaction, particularly under prefusion conditions. Among these, Annexins A2, A5, and A6 were found to colocalize with Myomaker at the myoblast plasma membrane. Proximity ligation assays further confirmed the close association of these Annexins with Myomaker at the cell surface. Functional analyses demonstrated that these Annexins can promote heterologous cell–cell fusion between fibroblasts and myoblasts. While single knockdown of Annexin A2, A5, or A6 had minimal effects, the simultaneous knockdown of all three impaired myoblast fusion, indicating functional redundancy among them. Together, these findings indicate that Annexins A2, A5, and A6 cooperate with Myomaker to promote myoblast fusion, providing a mechanistic link between the fusogenic machinery and membrane dynamics during myoblast fusion.

title: Revisiting atmospheric sulfur chemistry: Acid-catalyzed pathways do not control H2SO4 formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Sulfuric acid (H₂SO
                    4
                    ) drives new particle formation and radiatively important aerosol processes in the atmosphere, but its formation pathways remain poorly resolved because of limited kinetics data. To clarify these pathways, we combined coupled-cluster calculations, reaction rate theory, and a global chemistry transport model to quantify acid-catalyzed SO
                    3
                    hydration and its atmospheric significance. We find that the overall kinetics is not governed by a tight transition state but rather is controlled by a preceding loose transition state associated with the formation of the precursor complex of the acid-catalyzed SO
                    3
                    hydration. Our results reverse a recent view that acid catalysis is the dominant contributor to atmospheric SO
                    3
                    hydration, instead supporting an earlier view that water catalysis dominates SO
                    3
                    hydration. Incorporating the revised kinetics into the GEOS-Chem atmospheric model reveals no significant impact of acid-catalyzed SO
                    3
                    hydration on the simulated concentrations of H
                    2
                    SO
                    4
                    . The present findings highlight the critical roles of variational transition states in kinetic modeling.

title: Adaptive Ferroic Bi‐Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi‐Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI 5 (HBI) and HDASbI 5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi 0.5 Sb 0.5 I 5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1 H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.

title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d ‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3 d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d ‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d ‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d ‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d ‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

title: Correction to “Activatable Semiconducting Polymer Pro‐Nanomodulators for Deep‐Tissue Sono‐Immunotherapy of Orthotopic Pancreatic Cancer”
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: J. Li, N. Yu, D. Cui, J. Huang, Y. Luo, and K. Pu, “Activatable Semiconducting Polymer Pro-Nanomodulators for Deep-Tissue Sono-Immunotherapy of Orthotopic Pancreatic Cancer,” Angewandte Chemie International Edition 62 (2023): e202305200, https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202305200. In the original Figure 4b, the in vivo BL images in the SPpMB + US group were incorrectly placed. The error occurred during the figure assembly stage within file management software and is strictly limited to graphical presentation. They do not affect the underlying data, analysis, or conclusions of the study. The revised images are provided in the corrected Figure 4 below. Corrected Figure 4 We apologize for these errors.

title: Operando Identification of the Active Phase in Sr‐Promoted Lanthanum Cobaltite Perovskite‐Derived Catalysts for Ammonia Decomposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Storing energy in molecular form, particularly hydrogen in carbon‐free carriers such as ammonia, is considered a key strategy for future energy systems. The release of hydrogen via ammonia decomposition is a critical step in this context that requires scalable and economically viable catalysts. In this work, spray‐flame synthesis (SFS) was employed to prepare La 1– x Sr x CoO 3− δ (0≤ x ≤ 1) nanoparticles (≈ 10 nm), which serve as precursors for SrO‐promoted Co/La 2 O 3 catalysts prepared by exsolution. ESR, operando XRD, and ambient pressure photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provide insights into dynamic interfacial restructuring of the catalysts under the harsh ammonia decomposition conditions. The catalysts contain 25 wt% Co and achieve a maximum hydrogen productivity of 108 ·g Co −1 ·min −1 at 500°C for the La 0.75 Sr 0.25 CoO 3− δ ‐derived material. The coverage of La 2 O 3 with SrO/Sr─OH species under reaction conditions inhibits the migration of La‐based species, which block active Co sites in the absence of the promoter. An excess of Sr, however, promotes the growth of Co particles and reduces the exposed Co surface area. Beyond its structural role, operando APXPS reveals that SrO also influences reaction kinetics by facilitating NH x decomposition and weakening the binding strength of nitrogen, which is consistent with an electrostatic effect of SrO.

title: Rh0–Rhδ+ Synergy Enables Hydroxyl‐Directed Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Guaiacol
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin‐derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh 0 –Rh 0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh 0 ‐arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl‐directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic‐ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh 0 and Rh δ+ sites (Rh 0 –Rh δ+ ) were constructed in RhO x clusters through lattice‐oxygen‐mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron‐deficient Rh δ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π‐electron density. This hydroxyl‐directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh 0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back‐donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh 0 –Rh δ+ catalyst achieves a 2‐methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h −1 g Rh −1 , which is 22‐fold higher than that of Rh 0 –Rh 0 . Our findings establish hydroxyl‐directed aromatic‐ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin‐derived aromatics.

title: Zinc–Halide–Integrated Thermally Reprocessable Molecular–Emitter Supramolecular Glass Scintillators for High–Resolution X–Ray Imaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Transparent glass scintillators suppress grain−boundary scattering, but in many metal−halide glasses x−ray attenuation and terminal emission originate from the same local coordination unit, making their optimization mutually constraining. Here, we report molecular−emitter supramolecular glasses that functionally partition these roles between an organic phosphonium chromophore and a stoichiometrically incorporated zinc–halide environment. The phosphonium salt melt quenching methyl(4−(diphenylamino)phenyl)diphenylphosphonium iodide ( o ‐TNP) with ZnX 2 (X = Cl, Br, or I) and a trace amount of 4,4′−bipyridine (BP) produced transparent amorphous materials with glass−transition temperatures above 100°C. Across the halide series, the principal emission maximum remained within 493–500 nm, whereas the photoluminescence quantum yield increased from 3.53% to 10.01%, the average long−lived emission lifetime decreased from 9.7 to 4.4 µs, and the attenuation−corrected light yield rose from 14 909 to 22 954 photons MeV −1 . The optimized TNP−ZnI 2 screen achieved a system spatial resolution of 28.4 lp mm −1 at a thickness of 650 µm. After ten fragment−soften−recast cycles at 220°C, it retained 84% of its initial radioluminescence while preserving the emission maximum and spectral profile. This work provides a modular route for functional partitioning x−ray attenuation and long‐lived excited‐state dynamics with minimal perturbation of terminal emission energy.

title: Heterointerfacial Bonding Governs Service Stability in Flexible Perovskite Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The service stability of flexible perovskite solar module (FPSM) is contingent upon the bonding strength and stress‐response behavior at heterointerfaces. However, the fullerene‐based layer mainly relies on weak non‐covalent interactions. This makes it difficult for the FPSM to tackle the challenges posed by the coupling of multiple stresses in the actual service environment. Through the blending strategy of the polyamide curing agent and fullerene derivatives, we constructed an active energy‐dissipating multi‐bond network featuring covalent bond anchoring and hydrogen bond dissipation, which significantly enhanced the interfacial bonding and energy dissipation capabilities. Based on this strategy, a 100 cm 2 FPSM achieves a recorded power conversion efficiency of 22.33% (certified 21.5%). More importantly, for the first time, we developed an in situ bending electroluminescence experiment for FPSM under ultraviolet irradiation. After 5000 consecutive bending cycles, there was no significant decline in the module's performance, which verified its service stability under multi‐field coupling.

title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox in Polycrystalline Li‐Rich Layered Cathodes via Efficient Grain Boundary Passivation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage cathodes with hybrid anion and cation redox activities, such as Li‐rich and Mn‐rich oxides, offer a pathway to higher energy density in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, those cathodes suffer from oxygen loss from both the surface and grain boundaries, especially in traditional polycrystalline cathodes with secondary‐particle morphology. Interfacial passivation is needed, yet uniform, high‐quality coating at both primary‐ and secondary‐particle levels remains challenging. Here, using a tannic acid‐assisted process, we demonstrate an in situ formed Ba M O 3− δ ( M = Ni, Co, and Mn) perovskite phase at surfaces and grain boundaries, offering effective passivation to suppress structural and electrochemical degradation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), soft X‐ray spectroscopy (SXAS) and resonant inelastic X‐ray spectroscopy (RIXS) reveal that the passivated grain boundaries effectively mitigate oxygen release, promote the retention of oxidized oxygen within the grains, and improve oxygen‐redox reversibility. The stabilization is facilitated by strong M ─O bonding at primary‐particle surfaces, improving energy‐density stability and mitigating voltage decay. The improved electrochemical performance results from the reliable coating method, which constructs sequential interfacial bonding along grain boundaries. Using earth‐abundant elements only, this process may offer high‐quality passivation for a variety of oxide cathodes used in LIBs and beyond.

title: Spin‐State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon‐free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy‐intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐derived Co 3 O 4 electrocatalyst (MD‐Co 3 O 4 ) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co‐MOF‐74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability for the electrosynthesis of NH 3 from nitrate, along with robust activity over a wide pH and nitrate concentration range. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the oxygen vacancies generated during MOF pyrolysis induce coordination distortion of octahedral Co sites, leading to a high‐spin state transition with an electron‐rich configuration that synergistically enhances nitrate adsorption and interfacial electron transfer, thereby boosting the intrinsic activity. Moreover, this MOF‐based strategy is applicable to other M 1 Co 2 O 4 spinels, which provides an effective approach for spin engineering at the atomic scale and sustainable ammonia synthesis.

title: Monolithically 3D‐Printed Spectral‐Spatial Meta‐Authenticators
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface holography can encode multiple independent images in a single flat element, yet simultaneous operation at several visible wavelengths has typically relied on geometric‐phase elements, which require a prescribed circular polarization and bulky polarization optics, and on high‐index dielectrics that can suffer from visible‐band absorption. Here, we demonstrate a monolithically 3D‐printed, low‐index, height‐coded metasurface that performs polarization‐insensitive, broadband holography across spectral (wavelength) and spatial (near‐ and far‐field) channels. The propagation phase accumulated by each resin pillar is set by its height, so a single height map fixes the phase response at every wavelength at once and acts as a multi‐wavelength phase library. The symmetric pillar cross‐section removes the dependence on input polarization, and the transparent resin keeps the response low‐loss across the visible band. A fabrication‐aware optimization folds the discrete height levels imposed by two‐photon‐lithography slicing directly into the loss, so the design is printed as optimized in a single continuous step, without post‐optimization rounding. Experimentally, the device reconstructs a far‐field image that is read directly as a public key together with wavelength‐ and distance‐selective near‐field images that act as locked passwords, realizing a compact, dual‐credential optical authentication scheme under unpolarized illumination without polarization optics.

title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade‐off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge‐transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge‐transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT‐COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low‐temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy‐level alignment with structural conjugation.

title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO 2 /N 2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO 2 /N 2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR ( 1 H‐ 13 C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO 2 /N 2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH 2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO 2 /N 2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO 2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

title: Chemical Inhibition of Pyocyanin Biosynthesis Attenuates Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram‐negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the double‐layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small‐molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram‐positive bacteria, and identified a potent β‐lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity‐based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site‐directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X‐ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well‐defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa .

title: Gradient Mg and Uniform Ti Co‐Doping Suppresses Jahn–Teller Effect in LMFP via Optimized Ion‐Transport Kinetics and Interfacial Reactions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP), an olivine‐type cathode material, is gaining attention in high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries due to its high operating voltage and cost‐effectiveness. However, its practical use is limited by slow Li + diffusion, poor electronic conductivity, and structural degradation caused by Jahn–Teller distortion from Mn 3+ . To tackle these challenges, we have developed a dry‐and‐wet synthesis method to produce Mg/Ti co‐doped LMFP (Mg/Ti‐LMFP). This approach ensures uniform Ti 4+ doping at Fe sites and gradient Mg 2+ doping at Li sites. Ti 4+ strengthens the structural stability by forming M─O bonds, reducing Jahn–Teller distortion. Additionally, surface‐enriched Mg 2+ creates a protective layer, preventing manganese dissolution and electrolyte decomposition. The optimized structure and chemistry enhance Li + transport kinetics, stability, electronic conductivity, and cycling durability. Mg/Ti‐LMFP demonstrates 88.7% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C (25°C) and 88.2% after 100 cycles at 1C (55°C). This study lays a solid foundation for designing high‐performance co‐doped olivine‐type cathode materials, guiding the development of future energy storage solutions.

title: Threo‐Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo‐chiral cation additive of (2 S ,3 R )‐2‐amino‐3‐hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl‑induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral‑center threo‑configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically‑favored parallel‑to‑lattice multi‑site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective “lock‐and‐key” interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm 2 large‐area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high‐efficiency and ultra‐stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Polyacetylene‐Decorated Pt/TiO2 Catalyst for Highly Selective Hydrogenation of Alkynes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Supported Pt nanoparticles (NPs) and Pt single atoms (SAs) are widely employed in the selective hydrogenation of various fine chemicals, where Pt NPs typically deliver high activity while Pt SAs afford exceptional selectivity. Integrating these advantages into a unified catalytic system to reconcile the trade‐off between activity and selectivity in alkynes hydrogenation remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel Pt/TiO 2 ‐200C 2 H 2 catalyst featuring both Pt NPs and Pt SAs active sites was prepared via a simple and mild C 2 H 2 pretreatment. The C 2 H 2 monomer undergoes polymerization to form trans ‐polyacetylene (PA), which in situ covers the surface of Pt NPs and Pt SAs. The PA coating on the Pt/TiO 2 ‐200C 2 H 2 surface donates electrons to Pt sites, promoting H 2 dissociation and activation, inhibiting sintering and aggregation of the Pt species, thereby significantly enhancing the catalytic activity and stability toward the hydrogenation of various alkynes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that the PA coating increases the hydrogenation barrier of styrene on both Pt NPs and Pt SAs, suppressing over‐hydrogenation and enhancing selectivity. This work not only offers a novel approach for fabrication of Pt‐based dual active site catalysts but also presents a scalable polymer coating for modulating the catalytic performance of alkynes hydrogenation catalysts.

title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80 + macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

title: From Lying to Standing: Anchoring Naphthoquinone via Pd─S Bonds on Pd Nanoclusters to Suppress Over‐Hydrogenation for Mild H2O2 Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H 2 O 2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π‐system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low‐valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC‐72 affords a catalyst that produces H 2 O 2 through sequential H 2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H 2 , 30°C), achieving 300 mmol g Pd −1 h −1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X‐ ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone‐type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic‐ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H 2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π‐system, spatially decoupling H 2 activation from aromatic‐ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone‐mediated H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS‐Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression
abstract: ABSTRACT Sepsis is a life‐threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)‐mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS‐eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non‐canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD‐knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS‐mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.

title: Processing Window Expansion Enables Uniform Crystallization in Scalable Ambient‐Fabricated Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Slot‐die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition‐to‐annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot‐die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ‐to‐α phase transition while suppressing non‐photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large‐grained α‐FAPbI 3 films with minimized vertical compositional gradient and reduced residual strain. The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy‐level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large‐area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS‐L‐3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000‐Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate
abstract: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (O l ) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal–oxygen bonds that restrict O l migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg 2 V 1.33 O 4 catalyst with Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + interfacial sites ( n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi‐metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm −2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + ⇌ Rh δ + ─O l ─V ( n +1)+ ), which endows the catalyst with effective O l migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking‐resistant CH 3 O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long‐term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol g Rh −1 h −1 for H 2 and CO, respectively, along with a light‐to‐chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi‐metallic, redox‐active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable O l ‐mediated photothermal catalysis.

title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π–π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF‐based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre‐synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS‐treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long‐term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.

title: Bacteria‐Trained, MnO 2 ‐Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on‐target off‐tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell‐based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform—trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO 2 nanoparticles (designated MnArmL‐trDCs)—endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano‐transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO 2 armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC‐II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS‐STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor‐draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL‐trDCs induce a pro‐inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti‐PD‐1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano‐engineering cell armor‐based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster‐Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.

title: Nanotube Encapsulation of Single‐Molecule and 1D van der Waals Magnets: Confinement‐Tuned Magnetism (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Confinement-Tuned Magnetism In their Review (10.1002/adma.74808), Salman Ullah, Afzal Khan, Rong Xiang, and co-workers have reviewed recent progress on the encapsulation of various air-sensitive single-molecule and 1D van der Waals magnets within carbon and boron nitride nanotubes. This protection of outer walls and confinement in nanospace suppress quantum tunneling, preserves fragile magnetic states, and enable electrical readout of spin information. Such synergies open new frontiers in fundamental magnetism while promising transformative applications in spintronics, quantum information processing, sensing, etc.

title: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter From Living Polymers (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter In the Research Article (10.1002/adma.74348), Glaucio H. Paulino, Yuhang Hu, and co-workers introduce “living origami,” in which folding is driven by the growth and remodeling of “living” polymer creases rather than conventional actuators. Unlike active materials constrained by fixed polymer networks and predetermined configurations, living polymers can continuously remodel their molecular networks, enabling repeated, virtually unlimited reprogramming of folding pathways, structural configurations, and mechanical properties.

title: Spatial Control of Light‐Responsive Proteins and Optogenetics Within Hydrogels via Volumetric Bioprinting (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Optogenetic Volumetric Bioprinting Merging optogenetics and biofabrication, light-based printers enable patterning biological events. In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74563), Riccardo Levato and co-workers report a multi-wavelength volumetric bioprinter that can print and activate multiple photosensitive proteins and gene expression circuits with spatiotemporal precision. Context-aware printing enables cell pinpointing and targeting. This technology has implications in tissue engineering, developmental biology, disease modelling, and 4D bioprinting. title: Polar Wurtzite NbAlN: A Transition‐Metal Nitride Alloy for Polarization‐Engineered GaN Heterostructures (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Polar Wurtzite NbAlN NbAlN, a polar wurtzite alloy, is introduced as a transition-metal-containing barrier for GaN heterostructures. The alloy contains coherent, nanoscale Nb-enriched regions while preserving the metal polarity of the host lattice. The resulting polarization field tunes the density of the interfacial two-dimensional electron gas, opening a route to transition-metal incorporation in polar nitrides without intentional doping. More details can be found in the Research Article by Atsushi Kobayashi and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74756).
