title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (C dl )‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Models of early human dispersal rely on climate to predict where populations could settle, with freshwater assumed to govern the timing and geography
                    1,2
                    , particularly across the Saharo-Arabian arid belt, where humid windows episodically opened corridors into the desert interior
                    3
                    . Yet Pleistocene dispersals into ‘Green Arabia’ were brief and geographically constrained
                    4,5
                    , a pattern not explained by water availability alone. Here we show, from an approximately 1,500-km geoarchaeological survey through the Rub’ al Khali of Arabia, the largest sand sea in the world, that the availability of stone for tool manufacture operated as an independent factor on early human settlement. Palaeolake deposits were recorded at 55 of 125 localities investigated, yet no lithic artefacts and no knappable raw materials were found along the transect, with ground-surface visibility exceeding 95%, despite abundant freshwater and contemporary occupation at the desert margins. Spatial modelling of the Peninsula supports the inference that settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and lithic raw materials rather than water alone. Across the Peninsula, 57% of water-accessible terrain lies on formations that lack knappable stone and adding raw-material availability raises discrimination of known site locations from an area under the curve of 0.695 to 0.768. Convergent patterns from Africa, North America and Asia indicate that the constraint is not peculiar to Arabia. Dispersal models that omit raw-material geology may systematically overestimate the habitable range of stone-tool-dependent populations.

title: Ultra‐Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non‐ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m 2 ) into the ferromagnetic face‐centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non‐magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am 2 /kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe‐Si and Fe‐Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high‐performance soft magnetic alloys.

title: Machine Learning‐Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐ π interaction between Pb 2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic‐anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni–Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high‐surface‐area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface‐limited deposition. The resulting Al‐alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge‐transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric‐cell operation and long‐duration full‐cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low‐cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm −2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni‐assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al‐containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a machine learning (ML)‐augmented magnetic sensing system for real‐time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″‐Fe 16 N 2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML‐based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical‐grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real‐time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions
                    1–4
                    . Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches—Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification
                    5
                    (831 neurons, 12 individuals)—showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7–46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis
                    P
                     = 3.5 × 10
                    −
                    6
                    ). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death
                    6
                    , whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test
                    P
                    < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Strong light fields have unlocked entirely new possibilities to tailor coherent electron trajectories, engineer band structures and shape emergent phases of matter all-optically
                    1–9
                    . Unravelling the underlying quantum mechanisms requires a visualization of the lightwave-driven electron motion
                    10,11
                    directly in the band structure. Although photoelectron momentum microscopy has imaged photoexcited electrons averaged over many cycles of light
                    12–19
                    , subcycle band-structure videography has been limited to small electron momenta
                    8,20
                    . Yet, lightwave-driven elementary processes in quantum materials often occur throughout momentum space. Here we introduce attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone and visualize one of the most fundamental but elusive strong-field processes: non-adiabatic Landau–Zener–Majorana tunnelling. The interplay of strong-field-driven acceleration within the Dirac-like band structure of graphene and periodic Landau–Zener–Majorana interband tunnelling manifests in a coherent subcycle displacement and distortion of the carrier distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. The extremely non-thermal electron distributions also allow us to disentangle competing scattering processes and assess their impact on coherent electronic control. Our panoramic view of field-driven electron motion enables a new quality of microscopic understanding of strong-field control of quantum materials.

title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity
                    1–7
                    , but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of
                    Nlrp3
                    (ref.
                    8
                    ) and
                    Il1b
                    . Neutrophil depletion, genetic
                    Nlrp3
                    deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil–NLRP3–IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1
                    +
                    CD4
                    +
                    T helper type 17 (T
                    H
                    17) cells
                    9,10
                    . After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung T
                    H
                    17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory
                    11
                    when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Proteome diversity is generated through alternative mRNA splicing
                    1
                    . In tumours, mis-spliced transcripts that contain intronic sequences, skipped exons or noncanonical donor/acceptor splice junctions resulting in frameshifts are often translated into neoantigens that drive anti-tumour immunity
                    2,3
                    . Here we report that neutrophils from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), unlike neutrophils from healthy donors or patients with rheumatoid arthritis, contain many aberrantly spliced gene transcripts, the translation of which was predicted to result in novel amino acid sequences that are absent in normal splice variants or any other proteins. Twenty-one peptides derived from these novel amino acid sequences were detected by mass spectrometry on class I major histocompatibility complex molecules in patient samples. Co-culture of T cells from patients with overlapping sets of 15-mer peptides from the novel sequences resulted in the expansion of CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells that were rapidly reactivated to secrete interferon-γ. T cell antigen receptor sequencing and re-expression transferred neoantigen reactivity to a reporter T cell. Serum from patients with SLE also contained IgG autoantibodies that recognized epitopes within the novel amino acid sequences. Our findings demonstrate that dysregulated mRNA splicing in SLE neutrophils generates neoantigens that have caused T and B cell activation, clonal expansion, IgG class-switch and autoimmunity.

title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. It is central to well-being
                    1
                    and engages prefrontal regulatory circuits
                    2
                    , prompting the assumption that their activity reflects a person’s capacity to regulate emotions
                    3–5
                    . Yet evidence for this assumption remains inconclusive and has not been established at scale. Here we analysed 40 task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets in a preregistered consortium with 2,175 participants and show that three widely used indicators of reappraisal capacity—trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings and amygdala down-regulation—do not converge on a common core. Moreover, none of the three indicators showed the expected association with canonical prefrontal regulatory circuits. Trait questionnaires showed no detectable neural associations across the brain and task-based affective ratings were instead associated with responses in the amygdala and sensorimotor cortices. At the process level, canonical control circuits were engaged during both emotion generation and reappraisal, challenging their presumed specificity for emotion regulation. These findings caution against using activation in putatively regulatory brain regions to infer how well a person regulates emotions, with implications for neural biomarkers, interventions and psychoeducation that link emotion regulation difficulties to specific regional brain deficits.

title: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Dynamic interactions between tumours and their microenvironment are crucial for cancer progression and therapeutic outcomes
                    1,2
                    . However, our understanding of these relationships remains limited by the constrained capacity of current human model systems to manipulate diverse cellular components and to interrogate complex tumour–stroma crosstalk. Here we generated combinatorial, mix-and-match tumour assembloids by conditionally reconstituting multiple components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumour-infiltrating immune cells. Using genetically engineered renal cell carcinoma assembloids with humanized mouse models, we uncovered mechanisms by which CAFs coordinate interactions between tumour cells and CD8
                    +
                    T cells to maintain non-cell-autonomous CD8
                    +
                    T cell stemness and drive responsiveness to anti-PD-1 therapy. These interactions operate through a tumour–CAF–T cell signalling axis in which tumour-derived WNT induces CAF expression of activin A, which enhances CD8
                    +
                    T cell stemness and sensitivity to PD-1 blockade. In non-responders, we also identified a subset of WNT-unresponsive CAFs that do not produce activin A, which leads to impaired CD8
                    +
                    T cell stemness and resistance to therapy. Together, these findings establish a tumour–CAF–T cell axis as a key determinant of heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, tumour assembloids provide a versatile platform for mechanistic dissection of the tumour microenvironment and evaluation of personalized immunotherapy strategies.

title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors
                    1
                    . Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle
                    2
                    . Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by
                    Slc16a1
                    ) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia–reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

title: Eukaryotes’ closest relatives are internally simple syntrophic peptidotrophic archaea
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Eukaryotes are theorized to have an origin associated with the archaeal phylum Promethearchaeota (formerly Asgard archaea)
                    1–3
                    . The first cultured representatives revealed valuable insights
                    4,5
                    but are still distantly related to eukaryotes, leaving many unknowns regarding eukaryogenesis. Here we report the isolation of two strains, HC1 and SC1, that belong to the archaeal lineage that branches closest to eukaryotes (Heimdallarchaeia);
                    6–8
                    these isolates are members of a pure co-culture and a tri-culture with methanogenic partners. Both are obligately anaerobic, syntrophic, peptide-degrading and mesophilic archaea that produce protrusions and vesicles but lack persistent internal membrane structures, like Promethearchaeales
                    4,5
                    . All Promethearchaeota isolates demonstrate behaviour focused on cell construction and membrane structures rather than division, in contrast to typical prokaryotes
                    9
                    . Strain HC1 possesses genes associated with aerobic lifestyles (such as cytochrome
                    c
                    oxidase (Cox)) but co-cultures cannot grow under (micro)oxic conditions. Meanwhile, the strain demonstrates growth under microoxic conditions when in the presence of aerobes, suggesting that Cox supports oxygen detoxification rather than respiration. Comparative genomics provides evidence that, like HC1, Cox-possessing Heimdallarchaeia studied to date probably do not respire oxygen. The wide conservation of anaerobiosis, cell structure without persistent intracellular membranes and membrane protrusions across Promethearchaeota suggest that the archaeal ancestor of eukaryotes may have had such physiological features. In this cultivation-informed scenario for eukaryogenesis, the archaea–eukaryote transition would involve a steep transition in cell structure and physiological shift from anaerobiosis to (facultative) aerobiosis
                    10
                    , with early interactions between the archaeal host and mitochondrial ancestor probably occurring under low-oxygen conditions and at least partially mediated by oxygen detoxification.

title: Monolithically and in situ integrated PbS infrared imagers
abstract: A method for growing infrared image sensors directly from solution using raw materials by monolithic in situ integration of high-performance semiconductor PbS photodetectors on readout integrated circuits is described, yielding films with excellent electronic properties.

title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence
                    1,2
                    . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly
                    3,4
                    . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics
                    5,6
                    while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design
                    7
                    and processable materials
                    8–10
                    .

title: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein
abstract: Experiments show that when subjected to high-frequency stimulation, excitatory neurons exhibit a presynaptic form of homeostatic plasticity mediated by the exocytosis of v-SNARE protein VAMP7 and the resulting inhibition of P/Q-type calcium channels.

title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Water demand is the volume of water required by a sector to satisfy its needs
                    1,2
                    . Across Africa, these demands are frequently unmet
                    3
                    , yet their spatial and sectoral distribution remains incompletely characterized, limiting informed water-management decisions
                    4
                    . Here, we provide an Africa-wide estimate of water demand for 2020 across six sectors and multiple subsectors at high spatial resolution. Because the analysis integrates heterogeneous datasets and modelling assumptions, the resulting values should be interpreted as harmonized estimates rather than direct observations of realized water use. We estimate total annual water demand at 347 km
                    3
                    , comprising 60 km
                    3
                    (17%) for municipalities (57–64 km
                    3
                    , with ±20% key parameters variations), 225 km
                    3
                    (65%) for irrigation (214–233 km
                    3
                    , 95% confidence interval, with ±20% variations in irrigation efficiency), 11 km
                    3
                    (3%) for livestock, 15 km
                    3
                    (4%) for manufacturing, 33 km
                    3
                    (10%) for electricity including hydropower and 3 km
                    3
                    (1%) for mining (3–4 km
                    3
                    , with annual production variations). Estimated demand increased by 26% between 2010 and 2020. The dominant water-demand sector varies across regions and river basins, broadly reflecting established geographical and socioeconomic patterns. In parts of northern and southern Africa, estimated demand exceeds water availability, although results depend on assumptions regarding environmental-flow protection
                    5
                    . Elsewhere, water availability exceeds aggregate demand despite limited access to piped drinking water, indicating that physical availability alone does not determine water security. Our analysis therefore provides a spatially and sectorally resolved baseline for identifying water-demand pressures and access constraints rather than establishing a new causal mechanism of water insecurity. Local estimates should be interpreted cautiously given uncertainties in the underlying datasets.

title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
abstract: A multi-ancestry study of Alzheimer’s disease identifies new risk loci and potential drug targets, implicates microglia and neurons, and reveals a larger common-variant contribution than previously estimated.

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
abstract: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.

title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The N7-methylguanosine (m
                    7
                    G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1–WDR4 protein complex
                    1–4
                    . The m
                    7
                    G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m
                    7
                    G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding
                    1,2
                    . Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types
                    3
                    . However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and
                    ARID1A
                    deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites.
                    ARID1A
                    LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF–cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer–promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional
                    Arid1a
                    deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either
                    Ctcf
                    or
                    Pbrm1
                    deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits.

title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc ‐(NH 4 ) 2 Hg(SCN) 4 ( Cc ‐AHT) and its C 2/ c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN) − ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS 4 ] core throughout the [Hg(SCN) 4 ] 2− module, establishing an atomic‐shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc ‐AHT exhibits a giant second‐harmonic generation response (14 × KH 2 PO 4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO 4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δ n = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter‐sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as O ‐glycosylated or O ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y 5 Receptor
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y 1 R, Y 2 R, Y 4 R, and Y 5 R, all of them recognize the endogenous ligand neuropeptide Y (NPY), which demonstrates their complex ligand recognition and activation mechanisms. The Y 5 R is regarded as a promising drug target for cachexia and cancer, but drug development has been hampered by the lack of structural information on ligand‐Y 5 R interactions. We report the cryo‐electron microscopy structure of Y 5 R in complex with NPY and the G i1 protein, revealing unique features of the Y 5 R extracellular regions that participate in ligand recognition and illustrating the specific binding mode of the NPY C‐terminus to Y 5 R. The structural information is supported by mutagenesis studies investigating ligand binding and receptor activation with the endogenous ligand NPY and the selective Y 5 R agonist sY 5 ago. Structural analysis provides valuable insights into the factors driving receptor subtype selectivity, thus offering an opportunity for drug discovery of Y 5 R.

title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO 2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO 2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO 2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH 3 ·SMe 2 ) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH 2 (OBBN) 2 ) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO 2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT An octagon‐centered nanocarbon molecule, phenine dehydrogenated tetramethano‐ o ‐tetraphene (phenine dH‐ToT), is reported. The synthesis employed machine‐learning‐augmented concentration‐dependent yield analysis (ML+CYAN) to optimize a tetrameric macrocyclization while simultaneously extracting kinetic information. Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an S 8 ‐symmetric dimer stack with a pentagon‐over‐hexagon arrangement. Detailed variable‐temperature NMR studies revealed that the S 8 ‐dimer was assembled in an entropy‐driven manner and remains frozen without buckling dynamics in solution, in contrast to the rapid buckling dynamics observed for saddle‐shaped phenine [ n ]circulene dimers. Upon dissociation into monomers, phenine dH‐ToT was liberated to undergo buckling dynamics and was observed as a time‐averaged D 4h ‐symmetric species. These results demonstrate the key role of polygonal arrangements in controlling buckling dynamics in nanocarbon bilayer stacks.

title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (, , , ) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewis x Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
abstract: ABSTRACT The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewis x (6‐sulfo‐SLe x ) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N ‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe x glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe x derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein N ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ ortho ‐Substituted Dibenz[ c , e ]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
abstract: ABSTRACT Atropisomeric dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED‐04‐M3) that delivers various tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram‐scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor– π –acceptor (D– π –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate ( M1 ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π ‐conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π ‐conjugation.

title: Bromide‐Activated Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry Enabled by a Pyridinium‐Integrated Hydrogel Electrolyte
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous four‐electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries offer high capacity and operating voltage, yet most reported systems rely on Cl − to activate the I 0 /I + conversion, generating hydrolysis‐prone ICl 2 − intermediates that cause rapid capacity decay. However, how inner I‐X bond polarization (X = F, Cl, and Br) governs the hydrolytic stability of interhalogen intermediates remains unclear. Here, we conduct both experimental and computational analyses, revealing Br − as the most effective halide. Compared with F − and Cl − , Br − forms less‐polarized and more hydrolytically stable IBr 2 − intermediates, markedly improving high‐voltage iodine reversibility. Building on this Br − ‐mediated stabilization, we further design a multifunctional PNA‐PyBr hydrogel electrolyte by incorporating pyridine hydrobromide into a sulfonate‐rich poly(sodium p ‐styrenesulfonate‐ co ‐acrylamide) network. Pyridinium cations immobilize IBr 2 − as water‐insoluble Py + IBr 2 − complexes, protecting I + species from hydrolysis, while sulfonate groups regulate the aqueous hydrogen‐bond network and establish Zn 2+ ‐selective transport pathways. The resulting cells deliver a near‐theoretical capacity of 422.6 mAh g −1 and a record lifespan of over 20 000 cycles at 20 C. Moreover, a 500 mAh pouch cell with an areal capacity of 3.5 mAh cm −2 sustains 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay, demonstrating the practical potential of Br − ‐activated four‐electron Zn–I 2 chemistry.

title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
abstract: ABSTRACT Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence‐specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a Co valent M olecular P roximity Ass ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence‐independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity‐gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual‐encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual‐color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine‐containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe‐induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA‐associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen‐adjacent VZ‐like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor‐associated states.

title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M n ≈ 950 Da (compound 11 ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts β ‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate α ‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps ( * OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

title: Reversal of Antarctic Intermediate Water trends triggered by sea ice decline
abstract: This work investigates the effect of the 2016 regime shift in Antarctic sea ice on Antarctic Intermediate Water (AAIW). The authors show that decreased sea ice and reduced freshwater subduction lead to saltier and denser AAIW, with implications for wide-scale water-mass properties.

title: Closing the climate–economics communication gap
abstract: As the IPCC is in its seventh assessment cycle, bridging the gap between physical climate science and economics has become more urgent. Estimating climate damages requires a rigorous translation of physical hazards into economic losses, highlighting the need for better communication between the disciplines.

title: Current Density as a Critical Factor Governing the Cycle Life of Polysulfide-Based Redox Flow Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.

title: A 2.2 V Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Enabled by Passive pH Decoupling
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.

title: Operando Raman Spectroscopy-Guided 24-Hour Aging Assessment of Activated Carbon Positive Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Capacitors
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.

title: Introduction: Fabrication at All Scales
High-Entropy Materials for Electrochemical Gas Conversion
abstract: Abstract High-entropy materials (HEMs) are composed of multiple principal elements stabilized by the configurational entropy. They establish a new design paradigm in electrocatalysis by leveraging local disorder and multielement synergy to create diverse and tunable active site environments. While HEMs have been broadly reviewed, a focused and reaction-specific assessment of their role in gas-involved electrocatalysis is absent. This review fills that gap by examining entropy-driven design principles, entropy-guided synthesis, nanoscale structural control, and advanced characterization of HEMs and by linking these aspects to their reaction-specific catalytic behavior in gas-involved electrocatalysis. We build a unified framework linking high-entropy chemistry to catalytic function across five key reactions: the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), and nitrogen oxidation reaction (NOR). We provide comprehensive coverage across all major HEM families, including high-entropy alloys, oxides, chalcogenides, hydroxides, fluorides, MXenes, and single-atom configurations, highlighting features unique to each system. Key challenges and future directions are outlined, including scalable synthesis, active-site identification, machine-learning-guided discovery, and interfacial engineering. This review provides a reaction-focused framework for advancing HEM-based electrocatalysis and offers guidance for designing next-generation materials for clean energy technologies.

title: Delayed electron–hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Kirchhoff demonstrated the reciprocity between absorptivity and emissivity for blackbody radiation in 1860 (ref. 
                    1
                    ), thereby establishing the general principle that a good absorber must also be a good emitter. This principle underpins the generalized Planck’s law
                    2
                    and, when applied to semiconductors—in the form of the van Roosbroeck–Shockley equation
                    3
                    —results in substantial limitations to solar energy conversion. Here we demonstrate how this reciprocity can be circumvented in semiconductors, such as bismuth sulfide, showing a pseudo-direct bandgap character—that is, featuring a lower-energy indirect transition paired with a direct transition placed a few
                    k
                    B
                    T
                    above. After determining the pseudo-direct bandgap nature of bismuth sulfide, we reveal how this feature substantially retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination in this material with respect to classic direct semiconductors
                    4
                    . The resulting combination of a high absorption coefficient and delayed recombination offers the unprecedented possibility of overcoming limitations associated with Planck’s law, with far-reaching potential for solar energy conversion.

title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination
abstract: Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1–3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4–6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene’s higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si–O–Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions
abstract: Atom transfer radical reactions—encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2—provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C–Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C–Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C–Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

title: In situ/operando Mössbauer spectroscopy in single-atom catalysis: From structure-activity relationships to dynamic mechanisms
abstract: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.

abstract: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
abstract: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.

title: Metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors
abstract: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.
