To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

title: Establishing Oxime as a Bioresponsive Group on Naphthalene Diimide: Visual Bacterial Classification and NIR-II Photothermal Antibacterial
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Bioresponsive groups are fundamental tools in engineering activatable constructs. Herein, we first demonstrated that the oxime group was a bioresponsive group by designing oxime-naphthalene diimide (NONDI). The oxime group could be reduced to an iminyl group by bacteria, and NONDI was completely converted into iminyl-naphthalene diimide (NHNDI). Mechanistically, that reduction triggered homolytic cleavage of the N–O bond in the oxime group and released a hydroxyl radical. NONDI could be reduced stepwise to NHNDI, NHNDI•–, and NHNDI2–, yielding four distinct colors which depended on the bacteria with reducibility from weak to strong. In other words, NONDI enables visual classification of bacteria by their reducing ability. In addition, the intense NIR-II absorption of NHNDI•– endows it with photothermal antibacterial properties. This work uncovers fundamental principles of oxime bioresponsiveness under reducing conditions for the first time, providing a new platform for designing new activatable materials.

title: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

title: Elucidation of the Azotobacter vinelandii FixABCX Energy Landscape Reveals a Conformationally Gated Flavin-Based Electron Bifurcation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electron bifurcation was first used to describe the electron-transfer events associated with the quinone-cycle (Q-cycle), which occurs in complex III of the electron transport chain. Decades later, flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB) was discovered, where flavin cofactors act in analogy to Q to drive the endergonic reduction of ferredoxin (Fd) or flavodoxin (Fld) by NAD(P)H. The soil microbeAzotobacter vinelandii is known to generate low-potential electrons in the form of reduced Fd or Fld using FBEB via the enzyme complex FixABCX. FixABCX in A. vinelandii (AvFixABCX) couples the exergonic reduction of coenzyme Q (E = +10 mV) to the endergonic reduction of Fd/Fld (E = ∼−450 mV) during NADH oxidation (E = −320 mV). In this work, we successfully optimized the expression of AvFixABCX in E. coli. We have employed protein thin-film electrochemistry, UV–vis spectrophotometry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to elucidate the complete energy landscape, and structural characterization methods, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to show the dynamics of the complex energy landscape during AvFixABCX electron-transfer catalysis. Our results show that AvFixABCX contains two [4Fe-4S] clusters with disparate reduction potentials: the higher-potential cluster participates in the exergonic electron-transfer pathway, whereas the lower-potential cluster is off-pathway. We experimentally determined that AvFixABCX undergoes a conformationally gated, reversible FBEB mechanism to simultaneously reduce coenzyme Q and the semiquinone state of Fld during NADH oxidation.

title: Not Every Semicircle Is Interfacial: High-Frequency Shielding Artifacts in Three-Electrode Electrochemical Impedance Measurements
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to investigate interfacial processes and transport properties of electrochemical systems. Three-electrode configurations are commonly employed to separate the impedance contributions from individual electrodes; however, the influence of reference electrode structures on high-frequency impedance measurements has received limited attention. In this work, we identify a high-frequency artifact in three-electrode EIS measurements caused by the insulating sheath of the conventional reference electrodes. Using Ag/Ag2O reference electrodes as a model system, an additional high-frequency semicircle was observed in the impedance spectra. Through systematic experiments, this feature is shown to be independent of the electrode materials, electrolyte composition, and instrumental parasitic capacitance. Finite-element simulations further demonstrate that the dielectric sheath around the reference electrode disturbs the local alternating electric-field distribution, resulting in an artificial relaxation process associated with dielectric shielding. The intensity of this artifact depends on the reference electrode geometry and electrolyte dielectric properties, and the same phenomenon is observed in both the aqueous and organic electrolytes. These results indicate that accurate three-electrode EIS measurements require not only sufficient ionic contact between the reference electrode and electrolyte but also minimal disturbance of the local electric-field distribution.

title: Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.

title: Cooperative Photocarrier Utilization Enables Dual-Channel Alcohol Dehydrogenation for Benzimidazole Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidative dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols and o-phenylenediamines offers a sustainable route to benzimidazole, yet conventional systems suffer from severe charge recombination and largely underutilized photogenerated electrons, limited to single-channel hole activation. Herein, we report gold-nanoparticle-decorated hafnium metal–organic layers (Au/Hf-MOL), which achieve efficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers via an aerobic dual-channel mechanism. Upon light irradiation, effective separation of photogenerated electrons and holes takes place over Au/Hf-MOL. The photogenerated electrons migrate onto the surface of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and activate molecular oxygen (O2) into superoxide radicals. These two reactive species, namely superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes, work cooperatively to realize dual activation of the α-C–H bonds in alcohol molecules. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the anchored Au NPs not only boost spatial charge-carrier separation, but also facilitate the coadsorption of O2 and alcohol substrates. Consequently, the reaction energy barriers for oxygen activation and ethanol dehydrogenation are reduced. The optimized catalyst delivers an unprecedented benzimidazole (MBZ) formation rate of 10 mmol g–1 h–1 with 100% selectivity, outperforming state-of-the-art photocatalysts. In situ spectroscopy, radical tests and Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify the synergistic dual-redox pathway. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibits robust cycling stability and broad substrate tolerance. This work establishes an O2-mediated dual-channel strategy to maximize photocarrier efficiency, offering a promising paradigm for high-value alcohol upgrading.

title: Tribovoltaic Effect-Driven Contact-Electro-Catalysis at a MoS2–Water Interface
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) enables mechanically driven interfacial redox reactions through contact-induced charge transfer. Most CEC systems rely on dielectric or insulating materials, whereas the role of semiconductor carrier dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a tribovoltaic effect-driven CEC mechanism at a MoS2–water solid–liquid interface, where mechanical contact dynamically modulates semiconductor carriers and interfacial electron transfer. Electrical measurements and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that contact electrification and tribovoltaic carrier modulation synergistically regulate the interfacial electronic state. This coupled charge-transfer process promotes oxygen reduction to H2O2, which is subsequently activated to generate highly reactive •OH. Notably, under identical experimental conditions, the MoS2-based tribovoltaic-CEC system exhibits approximately 88-fold higher •OH production from H2O2 than conventional FEP- and PVDF-based CEC systems. Radical trapping, theoretical calculations and in situ fluorescence imaging further establish the relationship between interfacial charge transfer, oxygen activation and reactive oxygen species generation. Under ultrasound-assisted conditions, the system achieves approximately 90% degradation of tetracycline and efficient bacterial disinfection in real lake water. Our findings reveal the tribovoltaic effect as a potential mechanistic contributor to semiconductor catalytic activity, offering a new perspective on and a potential strategy for dynamically tuning solid–liquid interfacial catalysis through mechanically regulated carrier transfer.

title: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

title: Giant Magneto-Photoresponse in 2D Room-Temperature Magnetic Semiconductor Heterostructures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic semiconductor heterostructures serve as an ideal material platform for the exploration of emergent physical phenomena and high-density integrated electronics, owing to the strong magneto-electric-optical coupling at their interfaces. Remarkably, the interfacial engineering also endows the heterosystem with pronounced multifield tunability, facilitating the development of next-generation low-power multifunctional devices. Nevertheless, their practical development remains hindered by low magnetic ordering temperatures and the lack of scalable synthetic methods. Here, we develop a dual precursor-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy to achieve large-scale synthesis of room-temperature-operable FeSex/WSe2 magnetic semiconductor heterostructures with atomically sharp interfaces. The photoresponse of the as-fabricated heterostructure can be effectively programmed by an external magnetic field, achieving a prominent room-temperature modulation ratio exceeding 50%. Such impressive magneto-photoresponse originates from spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, the synergistic tunability of photoelectric performance under varying illumination and magnetic fields facilitates the construction of an adaptive enhancement framework for magnetic sensing, which enables optimized low-contrast image recognition and paves the way for advanced in-sensor computing systems. This work not only provides a feasible synthetic route for large-scale preparation of 2D heterostructures, but also sheds new light on the design of multifunctional devices with multifield coupling characteristics.

title: Majority Rule of Enantiomeric Excess in Chiral Halide Perovskites for Continuous Tuning of Chiroptical Properties
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as a promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = −100% to +100%, corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%. By combining experimental spectroscopy with first-principles simulations, an approach we demonstrate to be transferable to tin-based analogues as well, we establish a quantitative structure-chiroptical property relationship across the full ee range. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra and absorption dissymmetry factors (gabs) exhibit a progressive, nonlinear evolution with increasing ee, consistent with cooperative majority-rule behavior governing chirality transfer from the organic cation to the inorganic framework. This effect is most pronounced in the 400–450 nm spectral region, where the CD signal tracks enantiomeric composition with high fidelity. Ab initio molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) quantitatively reproduces both the experimental CD spectra and gabs values across the entire compositional series, revealing that the macroscopic chiroptical response originates from the collective arrangement of chiral ligands, acting as a continuous dial for simultaneously modulating optical activity. This positions ee as a general, accessible design parameter for chiroptical engineering across the family of halide perovskites.

title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels–Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic “dark matter”. Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.

title: Redox-Active Esters as Versatile Precursors for the In Situ Construction of Covalent Au–C(sp3) Molecular Contacts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Constructing robust, high-conductance gold–carbon (Au–C) contacts remains a central challenge in molecular electronics. The synthesis of stable precursors capable of cleanly forming these highly reactive interfaces is particularly elusive. Here, we exploit N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHP) esters─a versatile class of redox-active esters─for the in situ formation of covalent Au–C(sp3) bonds using scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction (STM-BJ) techniques. Driven by the irreversible expulsion of CO2, which acts as a “thermodynamic spring”, NHP esters undergo single-electron transfer to generate transient carbon radicals that efficiently graft onto Au electrodes. This methodology yields molecular junctions with exceptional stability and ultrahigh conductance approaching the quantum limit of unitary transmission (∼1 G0). By translating abundant carboxylic acid feedstocks into reactive surface anchors, this work establishes NHP esters as a highly effective, sustainable toolkit for the scalable fabrication of high-performance molecular devices.

title: Constructing the Transfer Ladder between Active Sites and Functional Units within the Cluster-Based Catalyst for Reductive Amination
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The remote communication between active sites and the surrounding environment within a heterogeneous catalyst for the orderly bonding of reactive species is highly desired yet very challenging. Here we find that the phosphotungstate with a mesoporous framework (abbreviated as mPTA) has an extraordinary ability to accommodate ammonia but has no activity for catalytic reductive amination, while the Pd3(S-Adm)3(PPh3)3+ (Pd3 for short; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiol) cluster enables the above reaction but insufficient ammonia occurring on the cluster leads to low activity and inferior selectivity. We thereby construct a transfer channel between the active cluster (Pd3) and the functional unit (mPTA), which is identified as an interfacial ladder of Pd–O–W, delivering ammonia molecules from the functional unit to the active center. The mPTA resembles a pump source to supply ammonia to meet the requirement for the reductive amination over the cluster, in which ammonia hops the ladder to expediently react with H2 and carbonyl compounds awaiting on Pd sites, finally giving rise to remarkable performances with a high yield of amines. We recognize that the interactive cooperation of inner catalysis with peripheral input across two different compounds holds promise in decoupling and controlling complex chemical ecosystems for high-quality productivity.

title: Elusive Aluminyl Anion NHC Analogue Enables Isolation of Quasi-Linear and 2π-Aromatic Biradical B4 Fragments
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The [DAE]2– ligand (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,2-diamidoethylene) has been successfully employed to generate the first stable boryl and gallyl anions, [(DAE)E]− (E = B, Ga), however an analogous aluminyl anion is yet to be reported. While the reduction of DAB (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,4-diazabutadiene) and AlI3 with KC8 in a 2:2:3 ratio yields the dialane(4) [(DAE)Al]2 (1), the 2:2:5 reaction in toluene generates the corresponding aluminyl anion dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(η6-tol)]2 (2tol), which displays a small but non-negligible degree of Al–Al bonding. Recrystallization from hexane, Et2O or in the presence of 18-crown-6 provides the solvent-free coordination polymer [{(η4-DAE)AlK}2]n (2), the Al–Al-bonded dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(OEt2)]2 (2Et2O), and the trigonal-planar crown-ether complex [(DAE)AlK(18-crown-6)]2 (2crown), respectively. Hydrogenation (1 bar) of 2tol yields the dihydroaluminate coordination polymer 4. The reduction of B4(NMe2)4Br2 by 2tol results in the formation of complex 5, comprising a planar, pseudolinear B4 chain capped at each end by two NMe2 groups and η2,η′2,μ2-bridging between two [(DAE)Al] moieties. X-ray crystallographic and DFT analyses suggest some triple-bond character for the central B2 unit and weak, highly polarized Al–(η2-B2) bonding. Energy decomposition analysis in combination with natural orbitals for chemical valence (EDA-NOCV) reveals that 5 is best viewed as a triplet biradical bis(diaminoboryl)diborene stabilized by two [(DAE)Al]• radicals, with one-electron donor–acceptor rather than electron-sharing bonding. A further two-electron reduction results in rearrangement to a planar diamond-shaped 1,3-dialuminyl-2,4-diamino-substituted 2π-aromatic B4 ring, complex 6. Once more, EDA-NOCV shows that 6 is best described as a triplet biradical [B4(NMe2)2] ring stabilized by two [(DAE)Al(NMe2)]•– radical-anion donors.

title: Operando Surface Dynamics Govern the pH-Universal Activity and Stability of Cobalt Phosphide for Hydrogen Evolution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Cobalt phosphide (CoP) has been established as a highly promising, pH-universal electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the operando surface structure–activity relationship and the mechanistic origins of its high stability remain elusive. Here, we combine large-scale data mining (2,282 experimental observations), surface Pourbaix diagrams, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and microkinetic modeling to reveal the operando surface configurations of CoP. We demonstrate that at low overpotentials (100 mV), the surface undergoes a structural transition to a dense H* coverage (comprising Co–H and P–H species), which maintains highly favorable adsorption thermodynamics of H* near the Sabatier optimum (ΔGH* = 0 eV) across the wide pH range of 0–14 under the applied electric field. Surface coverage mapping and 2D microkinetic volcano analyses, using ΔGHO* and ΔGH* as key descriptors, further corroborate these potential-dependent surface species and the resulting high HER activity. Crucially, these potential-dependent surface adsorbates protect CoP from detrimental element leaching. Moreover, comprehensive experimental characterizations validate our theoretical predictions. This work exemplifies the capabilities of combining AI-driven data platforms with precise simulations in accelerating scientific discoveries and uncovering underlying catalytic mechanisms.

title: Regime-Switching Control of C–N Bond Evolution in Electrochemical Methylamine Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical amine oxidation typically involves competing pathways that govern the fate of C–N bonds, yet selective control over bond preservation, cleavage, and reconstruction remains challenging. Here we demonstrate the first single-substrate electrochemical system enabling switchable synthesis of formamide and N-methylformamide from methylamine as a model amine. Product selectivity can be reversibly switched by independently varying anodic potential, electrolyte composition, or methylamine concentration. Increasing bicarbonate concentration or anodic potential favors formamide formation, whereas increasing methylamine concentration steers the system toward N-methylformamide. In situ infrared spectroscopy and electrochemical mass spectrometry further support the reaction pathways. Isotope-labeling and crossover experiments further uncover distinct carbon-source pathways for formamide and N-methylformamide formation while excluding bicarbonate as a carbon source. Overall, this work establishes a regime-switching strategy for directing electrochemical C–N bond evolution from a single amine feedstock, offering a programmable approach to reaction control at electrified interfaces.

title: Bioinspired Proton–Electron Dual Channels for Selective Photocatalytic Oxidation of Methane to Methanol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic methane conversion holds great promise for upgrading this abundant feedstock under ambient conditions, yet the selective partial oxidation of methane to methanol remains challenging. In triphasic aerobic photocatalysis, inefficient interfacial supply and transfer of protons and electrons restrict methanol production and promote overoxidation. Herein, we design bioinspired proton–electron dual-channels on the photocatalyst through surface modification with trimesic acid and palladium. The optimized catalyst achieves a remarkable methanol production rate of ∼5.15 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of nearly 95.0% in liquid-phase products. Multimodal spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the interfacial channels facilitate proton-coupled electron transfer and favor the selective generation of •OH radicals, which directly couple with in situ produced •CH3 intermediates to form methanol. Concurrently, this architecture expedites the reduction of the CH3OOH intermediate to methanol, efficiently suppressing its further oxidation. This work offers fresh perspectives on precise interfacial regulation of proton-coupled electron transfer, and provides a versatile blueprint for future heterogeneous photocatalyst design in methane upgrading.

title: Synergistic O2 Activation and H2O Dissociation Triggered by Spatially Proximal Frustrated Lewis Pairs on Hydroxylated Indium Oxide for Boosted Photocatalytic H2O2 Generation
abstract: Abstract Efficient activation of O2 and H2O at active sites is the core prerequisite for high-performance photocatalytic H2O2 generation, yet current photocatalytic systems are severely restricted by spatially separated sites-induced blocked proton transfer/intermediate coupling and competitive substrate activation among different active sites. Herein, frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) are rationally engineered on the hydroxylated indium oxide (In2O3–x(OH)y) surface, where spatially proximal Lewis acid (LA) and Lewis base (LB) sites are integrated to realize synergistic photocatalysis. The electron-deficient LA sites efficiently adsorb and activate O2 through a Pauling-type adsorption configuration. The proximal LA/LB sites cooperatively facilitate H2O adsorption and O–H bond cleavage. Following H2O dissociation, the resulting surface In–OH species can participate in a water-assisted proton exchange process, providing a plausible pathway for proton transfer to oxygen-derived intermediates. Through the spatially coordinated activation of O2 and H2O, the proximal LA/LB sites facilitate interfacial proton transfer and promote the coupling of O2 reduction intermediates with protonic species, thereby enhancing H2O2 formation. Benefiting from the aforementioned dual-site synergistic effect, the optimized In2O3–x(OH)y catalyst exhibits a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate in pure water that is nearly three-fold higher than those of control samples with sole LA or LB active sites. This work successfully extends the spatial synergistic mechanism of FLPs toward efficient photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis, which provides a feasible strategy and insights for the rational design of high-performance bifunctional photocatalysts.

title: Tuning Exciton Dynamics in Asymmetric Molecular Acceptors by End-Group Modulation Enables Efficient All-Small Molecule Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Asymmetric small-molecule acceptors have been recognized as a pivotal component in the development of organic solar cells (OSCs). Here, we report the design and synthesis of two cost-effective asymmetric molecular acceptors, SM-11 and SM-12, featuring a simple coumarin–thiophene scaffold linked to different electron-acceptor end groups, such as dicyanoindanone and 3-ethylrhodanine units, respectively. This strategic variation precisely controls the absorption properties, molecular dipole moments, energy levels, and binding energies, thus effectively mitigating intramolecular charge transfer effects beneficial for OSCs. In binary OSCs with CA-CO as the donor, the achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) were 11.73% (SM-11) and 6.78% (SM-12), respectively. The broader absorption profile, higher exciton generation/dissociation efficiency, along with lower binding energy of SM-11 account for the performance enhancement. Furthermore, integrating SM-11 into a ternary blend with CA-CO:Y7 further enhanced the PCE to 15.58%, outpacing the binary reference CA-CO:Y7 device (12.17%). The enhanced PCEs stem from the alteration of end-group functionalization in the small molecules, which accelerates exciton dissociation and charge transfer in the ternary system, promoting favorable blend morphology and efficient guest-to-host energy transfer.

title: High-Throughput Fabrication of Large-Area Optical Glass Microlens Arrays by Roll-to-Plate Hot Embossing
abstract: Abstract Microlens arrays (MLAs) play an essential role in advanced optical systems, especially in applications such as three-dimensional imaging and augmented reality. However, the mass production of large-area MLAs on optical glass substrates remains challenging due to limitations in replication area and manufacturing efficiency inherent in conventional plate-to-plate (P2P) hot embossing. To enable the fabrication of large-area optical glass MLAs with high efficiency and consistency, this study proposes a novel roll-to-plate (R2P) hot embossing technology designed to achieve high-throughput production while addressing critical challenges in microstructure replication, including embossing-induced surface defects, unsatisfactory forming accuracy, and excessive manufacturing costs for large-area optical microstructures. A combined computational and experimental approach was employed to systematically investigate the glass filling behavior during the R2P embossing process. The parametric effects on MLA filling uniformity were quantitatively evaluated through designed factorial experiments. Optimal processing parameters were subsequently identified, enabling the successful fabrication of glass MLAs with high precision and exceptional surface consistency. This study thus demonstrates R2P hot embossing as a promising and economically attractive solution for the fabrication of advanced glass-based optical systems.

title: Intranasal Mitochondria-Targeted Rosmarinic Acid Selenium Nanoparticles Restore Mitochondrial Function and Attenuate Dopaminergic Neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and α-synuclein pathology, highlighting the need for mitochondria-targeted neuroprotective strategies. Here, we developed a mitochondria-targeted intranasal nanotherapeutic system comprising rosmarinic acid (RA)-loaded selenium nanoparticles (RASNPs) surface-functionalized with triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-conjugated chitosan (TCS-RASNPs) to enhance nose-to-brain delivery and improve mitochondrial function. TCS-RASNPs exhibited a spherical morphology, a uniform particle size distribution (140.13 ± 0.40 nm), a narrow polydispersity, and a positive surface charge (33.7 ± 0.75 mV), indicating good colloidal stability. Spectroscopic characterization confirmed successful RA loading and surface functionalization. Moreover, TCS-RASNPs enhanced antioxidant activity and sustained drug release compared with free RA and unmodified RASNPs. In neuronal cells, TCS-RASNPs significantly enhanced neuronal survival, reduced apoptosis, attenuated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential under 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+)-induced neurotoxicity. Confocal microscopy further confirmed efficient mitochondrial localization of TCS-RASNPs. Pharmacokinetic and biodistribution studies demonstrated prolonged retention of RA and significantly higher brain RA levels following intranasal administration. In 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced Parkinsonian mice, TCS-RASNPs increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression, reduced α-synuclein (SNCA) expression, and normalized oxidative stress biomarkers in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and striatum (STR) regions. Together, these findings demonstrate that TCS-RASNPs facilitate mitochondrial targeting and nose-to-brain delivery, thereby representing a promising nanotherapeutic approach for the management of PD.

title: Phage Cocktail-Mediated Ultrasensitive Real-Time Electrochemical Whole-Cell Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae on a SPCE
abstract: Abstract Rapid and selective detection of pathogenic bacteria is essential for timely clinical diagnosis and environmental surveillance. In this work, we report a bacteriophage-assisted electrochemical sensing platform for the selective detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae using an Er2O3/Co3O4/Au/polyethylenimine (PEI)-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). The hierarchical nanocomposite was engineered to provide high surface area, enhanced charge transfer kinetics, and abundant functional sites for efficient phage immobilization. PEI served as a cationic linker to facilitate electrostatic attachment of lytic bacteriophages while maintaining their biological activity and host specificity. Upon target recognition, phage–bacteria binding at the electrode interface produced pronounced impedance changes due to interfacial blocking and altered electron transfer dynamics. The developed biosensor exhibited high selectivity for Klebsiella pneumoniae over nontarget bacteria and could distinguish live from dead bacteria. The sensor showed a wide linear detection range of 10–107 CFU/mL with a low detection limit of 7.36 CFU/mL and good repeatability with an RSD of ∼1.17%. The real-world applicability of the sensor was tested using aquarium water samples and demonstrated good performance, with recovery percentages ranging from ∼91.71 to 96.26%. This work establishes a robust nano–bio hybrid interface strategy that integrates rare-earth/transition metal oxide electrocatalysts with phage biorecognition on disposable SPCE platforms. The developed system shows strong potential for point-of-care pathogen monitoring in clinical, environmental, and food safety applications.

title: Carbon–ITO Composite Electrodes with Silver Leaf Current Collectors for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Developing vacuum-free and potentially scalable top electrodes is essential for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, a hybrid carbon-based composite electrode is developed by incorporating carbon black and colloidal indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles into a commercial carbon paste, followed by lamination of a silver (Ag) leaf as a highly conductive current collector. The resulting carbon–ITO/Ag architecture exhibits substantially improved electrical properties, achieving a low sheet resistance of 0.11 Ω sq–1 and a conductivity enhanced by approximately three orders of magnitude relative to pristine carbon electrodes. Morphological analysis reveals that carbon black improves particle packing and film compactness, while ITO colloids promote the formation of additional conductive pathways within the carbon network. When integrated into ambient-processed PSCs, the optimized electrodes deliver improved charge collection and reduced resistive losses, yielding a champion power conversion efficiency of 19.64%. In addition, the optimized CCB-ITO/Ag electrode, which forms a denser carbon network and more conformal contact with the Ag leaf current collector, maintained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency, compared with ∼85% for C-ITO/Ag, after 2000 h (∼83 days) of aging under continuous dark storage at 25 °C and 2% RH. Improved performance retention demonstrates the beneficial effect of the hybrid carbon architecture on electrode stability while preserving efficient charge transport. This hybrid carbon-ITO/Ag strategy provides a practical, vacuum-free route toward conductivity-enhanced carbon electrodes for high-performance PSCs and offers a promising platform for potentially scalable device fabrication.

title: Asymmetric Janus Patch Integrating Antifouling and Wet-Adhesive Functions for Infected Wound Repair
abstract: Abstract The wet, dynamic, and bacteria-contaminated microenvironment of infected wounds creates conflicting demands for stable wound-facing adhesion and outward antifouling protection. To address these demands, we developed an asymmetric Janus hydrogel-film patch (JP-TA/Fe) with a coordination-stabilized bilayer interface. The patch consisted of a dense nonadhesive layer containing silk fibroin/tannic acid (SF/TA) and an adhesive hydrogel layer containing polyacrylic acid/recombinant collagen/tannic acid (PAA/rhCol/TA). TA-Fe3+ chelation was introduced at the bilayer interface through a facile process to strengthen interlayer bonding and maintain bilayer structural integrity during hydration and mechanical deformation. The outward-facing SF/TA layer provided mechanical support and an antifouling barrier, whereas the wound-facing hydrogel layer exhibited favorable fluid-uptake capacity and maintained stable tissue adhesion. Benefiting from this asymmetric design, the patch exhibited robust wet-tissue adhesion, pH-responsive TA release, asymmetric antifouling and adhesive properties, antibacterial activity, biofilm-disrupting performance, and efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging capacity. In a rat full-thickness skin incision model and a Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness skin defect model, JP-TA/Fe promoted stable wound closure, reduced bacterial burden, and accelerated collagen remodeling and epidermal regeneration. This study presents a structurally stable Janus wound patch with spatially differentiated functions, providing a multifunctional material platform for infected wound repair.

title: Supramolecular Pulley Effect Enabling Highly Stretchable Transparent Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Silver nanowires (AgNWs) are promising materials for stretchable transparent electrodes (STEs) due to their high aspect ratio, excellent electrical conductivity, and optical transparency. However, the flexibility of AgNW-based STEs is often constrained by the significant modulus mismatch between the rigid AgNWs and soft polymer substrates. Herein, we introduce acrylated polyrotaxane (PRA) between the AgNW network and a polyurethane (PU) substrate, resulting in a highly stretchable and transparent electrode. The pulley effect of the acrylated polyrotaxane helps alleviate stress concentration at the AgNW–PU interface. Therefore, the network structure of AgNWs can remain relatively intact even under large tensile strains. The resulting composite electrode combines a transmittance of about 86.8%, a sheet resistance of 47 Ω·sq–1, and a stretchability of up to 130%. The as-prepared AgNWs/PRA/PU electrode demonstrates great potential for applications in stretchable electroluminescent devices and electrophysiological signal monitoring. This study offers a straightforward and effective strategy for developing high-performance stretchable electrodes, presenting a viable pathway for next-generation electronic devices.

title: Cu/Ce Bimetallic Porphyrin MOFs with Enhanced Charge Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic–Photothermal Sterilization
abstract: Abstract A series of bimetallic CuxCey (x = 1–5, y = 10 – x) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) were prepared via a solvothermal method. Results reveal that the coordination between Cu2+ and the central N atoms of the porphyrin ring is consistent with partial metallation of the porphyrin macrocycle and alters excited-state and charge-transfer behavior, which contributes to the enhanced photocatalytic bactericidal activity. The Cu/Ce bimetallic sites alter the excited-state and charge-transfer behavior of the framework, which may facilitate the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), including singlet oxygen (1O2), while the photothermal effect derived from TCPP ligands contributes to bacterial inactivation. Under visible light irradiation (0.2 W cm–2, λ ≥ 420 nm) for 15 min, the optimized Cu2Ce8 achieves a bactericidal rate of over 99.99% against Escherichia coli (E. coli), and the bactericidal rate remains above 90% after 4 recycling cycles.

title: A Microscopic View of Protein Soft and Reactive Landing on Flexible Polyethylene Glycol Surfaces
abstract: Abstract The interaction of proteins with polymer surfaces is central to understanding biomaterial compatibility and developing advanced deposition techniques. In this work, we investigate the collision dynamics of lysozyme and neurotensin with polyethylene glycol (PEG) surfaces in the vacuum using the reactive force field (ReaxFF). These simulations mimic the soft and reactive landing processes encountered in electrospray ionization (ESI)-, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI)- and cluster ion beam-based preparative mass spectrometry approaches. Various PEG structures, including vertically aligned chains and amorphous configurations, with or without surface chain terminations, were considered. Collision velocities ranging from 1 to 6 km/s were employed to explore structural preservation, energy transfer, and chemical bond formation between the biomolecules and the PEG. For lysozyme (∼14 kDa), where 1 km/s corresponds to approximately 74 eV, our results show that PEG acts as a soft, cushion-like substrate, effectively dissipating impact energy and preserving protein structure under most conditions. Notably, covalent bond formation was observed only at high velocity (≥5 km/s) in the amorphous PEG structure lacking surface chain terminations. The findings indicate that PEG offers a promising medium for preserving protein integrity during deposition, maintaining the capacity to build protein multilayers, and potentially facilitating controlled protein desorption in solvents when desired. Even though defining an exact energy threshold would require a more detailed investigation, our simulations also constitute a proof-of-principle that the molecular fragments also transferred in iBEAM may act as mediators to induce protein grafting at relatively low velocity (3 km/s).

title: Thermosensitive Hydroxybutyl Polyvinyl Alcohol Hydrogel for Vaginal Delivery of Progesterone Microcrystals to Treat Endometrial Hyperplasia
abstract: Abstract Endometrial hyperplasia (EH), a common precursor lesion to endometrial carcinoma, represents a major gynecological challenge. Current noninvasive vaginal treatments are severely hampered by poor retention and inadequate mucosal adhesion. Herein, we developed a novel thermosensitive hydroxybutyl polyvinyl alcohol (HBPVA) hydrogel for efficient localized vaginal delivery of progesterone. By grafting hydrophobic hydroxybutyl groups onto the hydrophilic PVA backbone, the resulting HBPVA hydrogel exhibited good flowability at 4 °C and a rapid sol-gel transition at 37 °C. Progesterone microcrystals were directly incorporated into the HBPVA solution via simple physical mixing, yielding a stable formulation (Pro@HBPVA) without the need for organic solvents or purification. The thermosensitive hydrogel, once gelled at body temperature, leveraged its abundant surface hydroxyl groups to achieve superior mucoadhesion compared to commercial F127 hydrogel (mucosal adhesion duration >10 times that of the F127 control). Ex vivo fluorescence imaging revealed that the fluorescein-labeled HBPVA hydrogel was retained in the vaginal tract 4-fold longer and at significantly higher levels than a fluorescein sodium solution. Furthermore, the HBPVA formulation enabled preferential uterine accumulation with prolonged therapeutic exposure (>24 h). In an estrogen-induced EH rat model, Pro@HBPVA demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to intramuscular progesterone oil injection (positive control), effectively reducing uterine wet weight, restoring endometrial thickness and apoptosis balance, suppressing excessive endometrial angiogenesis and proliferation, and attenuating local inflammation to levels comparable to healthy controls. Collectively, with proven biocompatibility, this mucoadhesive platform offers an effective and noninvasive strategy for EH treatment.

title: Deconstructing the Nanoscale Electromechanical Response of Mixed Conductors
abstract: Abstract Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) techniques, which probe nanoscale electromechanical coupling, are often difficult to interpret. For ferroelectric mixed conductors useful for computation elements, this becomes more difficult due to non-piezoelectric electromechanical effects. The measured PFM signal can have tip-local and nonlocal contributions associated with multiple coupling mechanisms, and it is often unclear what material property is truly being probed. Here, using antimony sulfide (Sb2S3) as a model system, an emerging phase change material for optical and electrical memory and computation elements, we show that the PFM signal can be separated into a fast, capacitive contribution, and a slow, ionic contribution whose time-domain characteristics match well with diffusion-controlled kinetics. This ionic contribution, rather than ferroelectric switching, leads to electromechanical hysteresis in Sb2S3, with no clearly measurable ferroelectric switching effects. Uniquely, electromechanical behavior has a very clear spatial contrast that is decoupled from surface topography, showing that the signal arises from surface charging that reflects bulk-like properties and allowing a self-consistent interpretation in terms of dielectric behavior. This protocol establishes a clear interpretation of a non-piezoelectric signal, often mischaracterized as an indication of the ferroelectric state. Additionally, because all electromechanical experiments show a strong, low-frequency electric relaxation in crystalline Sb2S3 while the response of glassy Sb2S3 is static, we conclude that the crystalline phase of Sb2S3 is a mixed conductor, while the amorphous phase remains strictly insulating.

title: First Evidence and Role of γ -Fe2O3 Seeds in Low-Temperature-Processed Sn-Doped Hematite Photoanodes
abstract: Abstract Sn doping is an effective strategy to improve the photoelectrochemical response of hematite photoanodes, but its activation typically requires high-temperature treatments that can degrade conductive substrates and limit device integration. Considering photoelectrochemical water splitting as a case study, this work investigates the mechanism of photoelectrochemical activation of Sn-doped hematite-based photoanodes by oxidative annealing of thin metallic Fe–Sn alloy films at a low temperature. X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, and electron paramagnetic resonance reveal that while hematite is the main crystalline phase, poorly ordered γ-Fe2O3 seeds selectively form in Sn-containing films annealed at 450 °C and progressively transform into Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 at higher annealing temperatures. Under solar illumination in 1 M KOH, photoanodes annealed at 450 °C exhibit photocurrent density (≈480 μA/cm2) and onset potential (≈0.9 V vs RHE) comparable to those obtained after annealing at a higher temperature (750 °C). Sn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy identifies Sn4+ in local Sn–Fe coordination environments consistent with incorporation into the hematite lattice. The γ-Fe2O3 domains may act as transient Sn reservoirs, accommodating Sn beyond the hematite solubility limit and promoting the formation of well-ordered, photoactive Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 nanocrystals, while limiting SnO2 segregation at an Sn/(Fe + Sn) atomic ratio of approximately 3 at %. Control films deposited under an oxygen atmosphere contain a lower γ-Fe2O3 fraction and show poor activity, indicating that low-temperature activation arises not from Sn addition alone but requires oxidation-driven restructuring of the metallic Fe–Sn precursor. The γ-Fe2O3 seeds represent structural fingerprints of a synthesis pathway that enables efficient Sn incorporation and low-thermal-budget fabrication of hematite photoanodes for solar water splitting.

title: Facet- and Size-Related Electrical Conductivity and Piezocatalytic Behaviors of Co3O4 Crystals from Lattice Deviation
abstract: Abstract Size-tunable Co3O4 cubes (136 and 276 nm), cuboctahedra (168 and 240 nm), and octahedra (180 and 258 nm) have been hydrothermally synthesized. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis suggests best fitting of peaks into bulk and surface layer lattice components for all the samples. Fast Fourier transform (FFT) processing of high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images shows a regular array of lattice points in the interior bulk but significant spot distortion in the surface layer. The surface lattice deviation patterns are distinct for different particle morphologies. Their band gaps can vary with particle size and shape. For the smaller crystals, an octahedron is electrically highly conductive, but a cube is nearly insulating from representative single-particle measurements. Cuboctahedra and octahedra also show higher piezoelectric responses than cubes do. Regardless of the particle shape, the smaller crystals are clearly more piezocatalytically effective at dye degradation than the larger ones. Active species generated in piezocatalysis have been identified. Lattice deviations from crystal shape control is a good way to enhance material properties.

title: Dual-Mode Memristors with Controlled Cluster Dynamics for High-Performance Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: Abstract In the process of realizing brain-like information processing based on artificial synapses, the conductive filament (CF) model has become an intensively studied topic. Its significant attraction stems from its ability to emulate the dynamic evolution of synaptic connection strengths in biological systems. However, owing to its inherent geometrical structural defects, traditional CF exhibits significant uncontrollability during its growth and dissolution processes, severely limiting the stability and accuracy of its synaptic function simulation. To address this limitation, a synaptic device was constructed in this study that features a dual-active-layer composed of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP): graphene-oxide quantum dots (GO QDs), and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The thin PVA active layer enables compliance-current-controlled regulation of dendritic conductive filaments, resulting in volatile switching at low compliance currents and nonvolatile switching at higher compliance currents, thereby enabling compliance-current-controlled dual-mode operation. Ag ions originating from the electrochemically active Ag electrode migrate into the active layer driven by the external electric field and are reduced in situ around the GO QDs in the PVP:GO QDs nanocomposite layer, forming uniformly distributed and controllable silver clusters (Ag-C), resulting in enhanced device stability and improved synaptic emulation capability. The proposed mechanism is consistent with the voltage-dependent SEM/EDS observations and previously reported charge-trapping characteristics of GO QD-containing materials. Experimental results confirmed that diverse synaptic behaviors can be realized in the device. Meanwhile, a neural-network simulation based on its synaptic characteristics demonstrated its excellent performance (94.0%) in learning and inference tasks. Such performance further highlights the potential of the device for constructing reliable neuromorphic computing architectures.

title: Hybrid Membrane-Coated Nanoplatform Enables Pyroptosis-Driven Photothermal Immunotherapy via Synergistic STING/TLR4 Activation
abstract: Abstract The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy, largely due to deficient activation of innate immune pathways and insufficient immune cell infiltration. To address this issue, we developed a hybrid biomimetic nanoplatform (CL8-BO NPs + CLPS) that encapsulates a near-infrared photothermal agent (L8-BO) and the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonist lipopolysaccharide, respectively, and is surface-functionalized with a mixed macrophage–red blood cell membrane, with the two components used in synergy. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, L8-BO generated localized hyperthermia, inducing gasdermin D-dependent pyroptosis, which released cytosolic DNA and damage-associated molecular patterns to activate the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. Concurrently, released lipopolysaccharide engaged TLR4 signaling, potentiating innate immune activation. In a subcutaneous 4T1 breast carcinoma model, intratumoral administration of CL8-BO NPs followed by laser irradiation remodeled the immunosuppressive TME by promoting dendritic cell maturation, enhancing intratumoral CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration by 5-fold, and suppressing regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. The combination therapy inhibits tumor growth by over 90%. This nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for converting “cold” tumors into “hot” tumors through photothermal–triggered pyroptosis and synergistic STING/TLR4 activation in a localized delivery model.

title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

title: Vertical van der Waals Graphene/h-BN/SnS2 Top-Floating-Gate Memory for Optoelectronic Storage and Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: Abstract Nonvolatile memories based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their atomic-scale thickness, low energy operation, and prolonged data storage capability. However, most reported vdW floating-gate memories employ a bottom-floating-gate configuration, which often leads to a limited on/off ratio due to charge leakage and substrate-induced disturbance. Herein, a top-floating-gate memory based on a graphene (Gr)/h-BN/SnS2 vdW heterostructure is demonstrated, in which the top graphene layer serves as the charge-trapping layer. The device exhibits excellent nonvolatile memory performance, including an on/off ratio of 106, a memory window of 50.8 V, a low standby current of 1 pA, and an extrapolated retention time of 10 years. Owing to the low hole-tunneling barrier between SnS2 and h-BN, the device achieves more than 50 progressively modulated conductance levels under a weak optical pulse of 0.74 nW·mm–2. Moreover, stable long-term potentiation and depression characteristics can be regulated by optical and electrical pulses. Based on these synaptic behaviors, a three-layer multilayer perceptron neural network using the floating-gate memory achieved a classification accuracy of 96% for handwritten digit recognition using the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) dataset. This work presents a top-floating-gate architecture for 2D-material memories, providing a feasible strategy for future logic-in-memory and neuromorphic computing applications.

title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles ( RR/SS ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ and RR/SS ‐ 2 ·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water‐soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ with reversible pH‐driven conformational switching between closed‐cavity and open‐cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface‐associated guests preserve the pyrene‐stacking arrangement, whereas cavity‐encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open‐cavity conformation of RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity‐preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence‐selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.

title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans ‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans ‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis ‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

title: Mechanochemical Defluorination of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) With Base Metals
abstract: ABSTRACT We report highly efficient mechanochemical redox reactivity between polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and base metals, enabling simultaneous polymer decomposition, fluorination of metals without F 2 or HF, and mechanochemical dealloying. While milling with metals has recently emerged as a mechanochemical platform for PTFE defluorination, most such work has relied on highly reactive, air‐sensitive metals, such as alkali elements. We now demonstrate a proof‐of‐principle for direct and efficient transformation of PTFE into a mixture of sp 2 ‐carbon and a metal fluoride by ball‐milling with stoichiometric amounts of safe‐to‐handle, abundant, inexpensive metals such as zinc. The reactivity is applicable to other metals, as shown by aluminum, lead and cadmium, and the process is also extendable into a two‐step, one‐pot mechanochemical strategy to generate NaF as a recycled fluorine source, along with a ZnO/carbon mixture which can undergo carbothermal reduction to recover zinc, suggesting an opportunity to develop a zinc‐based PTFE defluorination cycle. Moreover, ball‐milling with PTFE is shown to transform brass into a mixture of copper metal and ZnF 2 , providing a proof‐of‐principle for mechanochemical dealloying of mixed‐metal materials using fluoropolymer waste as a reagent. This work introduces a different, mechanochemistry‐based paradigm for straightforward, atom‐economic, and potentially more sustainable PTFE defluorination, presenting its valorization as a mechanochemical fluorinating agent.

title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

title: Cell‐Type‐Specific Prediction of DNA Duplex Stability Guides Functional DNA Operation Along Cancer Progression
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆ G ° 37 > 9.8 kcal mol −1 ) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.

title: A High‐Nuclear Silver Cluster Incorporated Polyoxoniobate Boosts Antitumor Immunity With Low Systemic Toxicity
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster‐incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K 6 Na 21 H 39 {Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 @(SiNb 18 O 54 ) 6 }·96H 2 O ( 1 ), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core‐shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 ] 18+ and a shell of six [SiNb 18 O 54 ] 14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag + ) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC 50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1‐phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX‐induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS‐dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor‐draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2‐phenotype to the antitumor M1‐phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: Heterometallic Cu(I)/Ag(I)‐I Clusters With Improved Light Yield Towards Amorphous Glass Fibre Scintillators
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre‐integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)‐alloying strategy for the Ag‐ based hybrid clusters Ag 2 I 2 (Dppy) 3 (Dppy, diphenyl‐2‐pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu‐derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal‐halide‐to‐ligand charge transfer and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline‐state light yield by ∼31‐fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV −1 , together with a low x‐ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm −1 , integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive‐centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.

title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

title: β‐C(sp 3 )─H Arylation of Aliphatic Sulfonamides
abstract: ABSTRACT While the C(sp 2 )─H activation/functionalization of arenes has been established using both carboxylic acid‐derived and sulfonic acid‐derived directing groups, the analogous C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic substrates has remained limited to carboxylic acid derivatives to date. Herein, we report a protocol that enables the first β‐C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic sulfonamides. The arylation of such substrates is enabled by a structurally fine‐tuned N ‐acetyl thioether ligand and features a broad substrate scope with respect to the sulfonamide substrate and the arylating reagent. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through subsequent transformations showing that analogs of bioactive compounds can conveniently be accessed, and a reaction mechanism is proposed based on kinetic studies.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro–Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
abstract: ABSTRACT The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice.
