Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem‐Cell‐Based Tendon Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D‐MRI with real‐time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering‐precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF‐mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC‐based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.

title: In‐Situ Self‐Evolving µ‐Sn 10 Bi Cross‐Interlocked Structure and Three‐in‐One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low‐Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e − /Na + transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn 10 Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn 10 Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: Life‐Cycle‐Sustainable Capacitive Deionization Enabled by Organic Molecular Engineering for Selective Ammonium Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective ammonium (NH 4 + ) recovery from complex wastewater streams remains a pivotal challenge in sustainable nitrogen management. Capacitive deionization (CDI) offers an energy‐efficient electrochemical route for ion separation, yet its practical application is constrained by the inherent trade‐off between NH 4 + adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we circumvent this fundamental limitation through the rational molecular engineering of an organic electroactive material, 1,4‐bis(1H‐imidazo[4,5‐b]phenazin‐2‐yl)benzene (IPB), which features extended electron delocalization and abundant C═N moieties for NH 4 + ‐specific redox‐coupled capture. The resulting IPB‐based CDI prototype delivers a high NH 4 + adsorption capacity of 267.23 mg g −1 and a fast rate of 62.51 mg g −1 min −1 , while sustaining remarkable selectivity in complex multi‐ion matrices, thereby effectively surpassing the conventional capacity‐selectivity trade‐off. Notably, CDI adsorption reduces wastewater NH 4 + levels to below 3 mg L −1 and achieves 82.3% direct recovery as liquid fertilizer during CDI desorption, as demonstrated by isotope tracing experiments. The CDI process exhibits a low carbon footprint of only 4.66 × 10 −2 t CO 2 ‐equivalent per tonne of NH 4 + treated, underscoring its superior life‐cycle sustainability. Therefore, this work proposes a molecularly engineered organic electrode material for high‐performance wastewater remediation and circular nutrient recovery, paving the way toward carbon‐neutral electrochemical water treatment technologies.

title: Synthesis of Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 x 2 InB 2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Biointerface‐Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria‐Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Ion‐Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All‐Solid‐State Li–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple‐phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface‐bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm −2 while delivering a loading‐insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm −2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface‐bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion‐electron transfer (CIET) in all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Nb 5+ ‐Induced‐CeO 2 Lattice Strain for Robust and Scalable Solar‐Driven Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia (NH 3 ) underpins fertilizer production and is emerging as a renewable‐energy carrier. Solar‐driven gas‐phase N 2 /H 2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H 2 ‐rich conditions. Here, Nb 5+ incorporation into CeO 2 contracts the lattice and induces compressive microstrain, suppressing excessive oxygen‐sublattice reduction and preserving Ru dispersion. In situ NAP‐XPS and computational results show that Nb‐CeO 2 maintains an electron‐enriched Ru working state under reaction conditions, which is further promoted by illumination. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb‐CeO 2 achieves an NH 3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g −1 h −1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N 2 ‐activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NH x hydrogenation and NH 3 desorption. Scale‐up synthesis affords a 3 wt% Ru/Nb‐CeO 2 ‐L catalyst stable for 480 h and operable under outdoor concentrated sunlight. A screening‐level analysis estimates a catalyst‐and‐feedstock cost of 286–322 USD t NH3 −1 under the lower‐bound electricity scenario, 42%–51% below the selected Cs‐Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar‐driven ammonia synthesis.

title: “Activation‐Resistance Elimination” Regulation by Lanthanide/Transition Metal Ion‐Coordinated Nanostructures Intensifies Cuproptosis and Tumor Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion‐coordinated nanoparticle, La‐Cu@Lap/IWR‐1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation. La 3+ not only enhances Cu 2+ ‐mediated multiple enzyme‐mimetic activities via coordination to amplify oxidative stress but also disrupts lysosomal acidification to improve copper ion availability. Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu 2+ , significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR‐1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β‐catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia‐inducible factor 1α (HIF‐1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial‐mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: Ionic‐Ligand‐Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg −1 Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI − anions, creating anion‐rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li + hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm −1 ) and an exceptional Li + transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid‐state Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high‐energy‐density (515 Wh kg −1 ) solid‐state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high‐loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm −2 ) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic‐ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance and high‐safety solid‐state batteries.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Use common standards to stop risky research
Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun’s arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF 2
abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.
